specs.title: ACL — Change Role
specs.summary: An authorized party moves a subject's AclEntry 0.2 from one role to another, with a compare-and-swap on the current role and the entry re-checked against the new role's ceilings.

specs.title: ACL — Grant
specs.summary: A granting authority adds a subject to an access-control list with a role, an explicit act scope, the purposes the subject may use what it reads for, and optionally an approve scope and a narrowed, qualified or additive capability set.

specs.title: ACL — List
specs.summary: A querying party asks an ACL maintainer to enumerate its AclEntry 0.2 records, filtered by role, by context or resource in an explicitly stated direction, and by capability, with paging.

specs.title: ACL — Revoke
specs.summary: A revoking party removes a subject's AclEntry 0.2 from an access-control list, or narrows its act scope to a stated, explicit narrower scope.

specs.title: ACL — Show
specs.summary: A querying party asks an ACL maintainer for the AclEntry 0.2 it holds for one subject — role, explicit act and approve scopes, and capabilities.

specs.title: ACL — Swap Key
specs.summary: An ACL holder atomically replaces the VID bound to one of their own AclEntries with a new VID — preserving role, scopes, and label, and closing the old VID's access in the same transaction.

specs.title: ACL — Update
specs.summary: Amend an existing AclEntry 0.2 — widen its act scope, or replace its approve, capability or key scope, label, expiry or step-up — leaving role changes to acl/change-role and act narrowing to acl/revoke.

specs.title: Audit — List
specs.summary: Page through a maintainer's append-only audit log, newest first, with optional filters and an opaque continuation cursor.

specs.title: Audit — Verify
specs.summary: Walk a maintainer's append-only audit hash chain and report whether it is internally consistent, locating the first break if it is not.

specs.title: Auth — Authenticate
specs.summary: A subject presents a challenge in a proof-bearing document and gets back a session + tokens. 0.3 lets a delegate (e.g. a holder's VTA) authenticate a principal on its behalf, alongside the 0.2 session-key binding.

specs.title: Auth — Challenge
specs.summary: A party requests a one-time nonce from an authentication service that they will sign to prove control of their VID.

specs.title: Auth — OOB Cancel
specs.summary: The starter or the lock holder of an out-of-band request ends it; a cancelled request is final and can never be approved or redeemed.

specs.title: Auth — OOB Claim
specs.summary: An approver's wallet claims a pending out-of-band request with a throwaway key, locking the request to that key, and gets back the service-signed step 1: which community, at which portal origin, for what purpose, and until when.

specs.title: Auth — OOB Grant
specs.summary: A member's signed decision on one out-of-band request: let this starter key act as me at this origin until sessionEndsAt, having seen this context, and sign these task families as me for that session — or decline. Signed for assertionMethod, carried only inside auth/oob/respond.

specs.title: Auth — OOB Identify
specs.summary: A member's DID states that it holds the lock on one out-of-band request and has entered the number shown on the starter's screen; signed by the member's VTA for authentication and carried only inside auth/oob/prove.

specs.title: Auth — OOB Prove
specs.summary: The lock holder proves membership and the number on the starter's screen by carrying a signed auth/oob/identify, and gets back the service-signed step 2: where the request came from, which key it would sign in, and which task families that key would sign for.

specs.title: Auth — OOB Redeem
specs.summary: The starter long-polls an out-of-band request with its own key and, once the member has approved, turns it into a session bound to that key; before approval it learns the request's state and, once claimed, the number to show.

specs.title: Auth — OOB Request
specs.summary: A starter, such as a browser on a portal page, asks a service to open an out-of-band request that an approver will decide on another device, and gets back the request's handle and the instant its claim window closes.

specs.title: Auth — OOB Respond
specs.summary: The lock holder of an out-of-band request delivers the member's signed decision by carrying an auth/oob/grant, and the service records the request as approved or declined; no session material ever comes back to the approver.

specs.title: Auth — Passkey Admin List
specs.summary: An administrator lists one member's passkeys of one purpose — typically their step-up passkeys — as non-secret metadata, so they can tell which to revoke. Never key material.

specs.title: Auth — Passkey Enroll (finish)
specs.summary: A subject submits the WebAuthn attestation that completes a passkey enrollment. The auth service verifies the attestation and binds the public credential to the subject's VID.

specs.title: Auth — Passkey Enroll (invite)
specs.summary: An administrator issues a single-use invite, redeemed with a separately delivered claim code, binding a passkey to a subject who cannot authorise it themselves — a first passkey, or a step-up-only passkey that never opens a session.

specs.title: Auth — Passkey Invite List
specs.summary: An administrator lists the passkey enrolment invites they have issued and that have not been redeemed — who each binds a passkey to, for what, and when it lapses — never the tokens themselves.

specs.title: Auth — Passkey Invite Revoke
specs.summary: An administrator withdraws an outstanding passkey enrolment invite, identified by its invite handle, so it can never be redeemed.

specs.title: Auth — Passkey Invite Update
specs.summary: An administrator changes an outstanding passkey enrolment invite's role or expiry, identified by its invite handle, without re-issuing it.

specs.title: Auth — Passkey Enroll (redeem, finish)
specs.summary: The invitee returns the new credential's attestation — and an assertion from an existing credential of the same purpose, where the subject has one — and the auth service binds the credential to the invite's subject, with the invite's purpose, and consumes the invite.

specs.title: Auth — Passkey Enroll (redeem, start)
specs.summary: The invitee presents an enrollment invite's token and its separately delivered claim code, and the auth service begins the registration the invite authorises, with a user-verification ceremony over the subject's existing credentials of the same purpose.

specs.title: Auth — Passkey Enroll (start)
specs.summary: An authenticated subject asks the auth service to begin a WebAuthn registration ceremony so a new passkey can be bound to their VID.

specs.title: Auth — Passkey List
specs.summary: A subject lists every passkey the auth service holds for them, so they can tell their authenticators apart before revoking one.

specs.title: Auth — Passkey Login (finish)
specs.summary: A party submits the WebAuthn assertion completing a passkey login or step-up; the auth service verifies the assertion and either issues a fresh session (login) or elevates an existing session's AAL (step-up).

specs.title: Auth — Passkey Login (start)
specs.summary: A party asks an auth service to begin a WebAuthn authentication ceremony — issuing PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions for either an initial login or an AAL step-up against an existing session.

specs.title: Auth — Passkey Revoke (finish)
specs.summary: The producer — the credential's owner, or an administrator acting for them — submits the user-verification assertion that completes a passkey revocation; on success the credential, of either purpose, is unbound permanently.

specs.title: Auth — Passkey Revoke (start)
specs.summary: A subject — or an administrator, for them — asks the auth service to begin removing a passkey of either purpose; the response is a fresh user-verification challenge for the person acting, satisfied before anything is removed.

specs.title: Auth — Refresh
specs.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new access token, without re-running the challenge-response handshake. 0.2 accepts a proof by the session key bound at login as an additional binding check, and never extends a session past its absolute lifetime.

specs.title: Auth — Revoke Session
specs.summary: A subject ends one of its sessions or all of them, or an administrator ends every session of a subject whose access it could withdraw.

specs.title: Auth — Sessions List
specs.summary: A subject lists every active session the auth service holds for them — typical "where am I signed in?" UX for users managing multi-device authentication.

specs.title: Auth — Signing Key Authorize
specs.summary: An identity's own signed authorization of one signing-key enrolment, carried inside auth/signing-key/enroll so a holder of the identity's key can authorize a delegation without a passkey gesture.

specs.title: Auth — Signing Key Enroll
specs.summary: A freshly generated key is enrolled as a delegation of an identity, so documents it signs are authorized by that identity's standing. The identity may authorize it with its own signature, and one enrolment may replace one of its active keys.

specs.title: Auth — Signing Key List
specs.summary: An identity lists the signing keys delegated to act for it — which devices can sign in its name, when each was last used, and which were revoked — so it can tell them apart before revoking one.

specs.title: Auth — Signing Key Revoke
specs.summary: Revoke one signing-key delegation, so the next document its key signs is refused — by the identity it acts for, or by an administrator doing incident response.

specs.title: Auth — Step-up Approve Request
specs.summary: A relying party asks a wallet or verifiable-trust agent to ratify an authentication step-up — issuing a challenge, and stating which kinds of evidence it will accept, including a statement by one of the subject's bound step-up approvers.

specs.title: Auth — Step-up Approve Response
specs.summary: An approver's answer to a step-up approve-request, backed by the approver's own evidence — a proof by its own DID, or a WebAuthn assertion by a passkey registered to it over the step-up challenge. A delegated key's proof never counts as the approver's.

specs.title: Auth — Step-up Approver Attest
specs.summary: A step-up approver's signed statement — for one subject, at one relying party, over one challenge, bound to one operation or enrolment — carried embedded in the document it backs, never sent on its own.

specs.title: Auth — Step-up Approver Enroll
specs.summary: A subject who already holds a step-up factor adds a step-up approver, or rotates one out, on the evidence of that existing factor and the new approver's signed proof of possession — without anyone else's help.

specs.title: Auth — Step-up Approver Invite
specs.summary: An administrator issues a single-use invite, redeemed by the invited subject with a separately delivered claim code, to bind a step-up approver to a subject who holds no step-up factor from which to authorize one themselves.

specs.title: Auth — Step-up Approver List
specs.summary: A subject lists the step-up approvers bound to them — or an administrator lists another subject's within its authority — so a factor can be recognised before it is replaced or revoked.

specs.title: Auth — Step-up Approver Redeem (finish)
specs.summary: The invited subject, signing as their own DID, names the approver to bind and carries its signed enrolment statement over the ceremony's challenge; the relying party binds the approver to the subject as their step-up factor and consumes the invite.

specs.title: Auth — Step-up Approver Redeem (start)
specs.summary: The invited subject, signing as their own DID, presents a step-up approver invite's token and its separately delivered claim code, and the relying party opens an enrolment ceremony with a challenge for the approver to sign.

specs.title: Auth — Step-up Approver Revoke
specs.summary: Revoke one step-up approver binding, so the next statement the approver signs is refused — by the subject it is bound to, or by an administrator acting on their behalf.

specs.title: Auth — Step-up Policy
specs.summary: The relying party's per-operation-class policy deciding whether — and how — a session must step up to a higher assurance level before a gated operation runs, plus how a system-wide floor composes with per-entry overrides.

specs.title: Auth — Step-up Request Show
specs.summary: The subject's approver agent fetches, by a single-use handle, a pending step-up — the relying party's signed approve-request and the operation it binds — so a step-up refused to a delegated producer can be answered on the subject's own device.

specs.title: Auth — Step-up Start
specs.summary: A session holder asks a relying party to begin raising the assurance level of one of its sessions; the relying party answers with the signed approve-request the approver then answers.

specs.title: Auth — Whoami
specs.summary: A subject asks an auth service to introspect the current session — returning the Session object, role assignments, effective scopes and effective capabilities — so the client can reconcile state with the server's view.

specs.title: Backup — Abort
specs.summary: Cancel an in-flight export or import bundle and discard its bytes.

specs.title: Backup — Complete Export
specs.summary: Acknowledge that an export bundle was downloaded, so the node can release it.

specs.title: Backup — Finalize Import
specs.summary: Decrypt an uploaded bundle and replace this node's state with it.

specs.title: Backup — Get Chunk
specs.summary: Retrieve one chunk of a chunked export bundle by index, over the transport that carries the rest of the family.

specs.title: Backup — Initiate Export
specs.summary: Mint an encrypted full-state export bundle and return the descriptor that fetches it, over HTTPS or chunk by chunk over the node's own Trust Task transport.

specs.title: Backup — Initiate Import
specs.summary: Mint an upload slot for an encrypted bundle and return the descriptor that writes to it, over HTTPS or chunk by chunk over the node's own Trust Task transport.

specs.title: Backup — Put Chunk
specs.summary: Write one chunk of a chunked import bundle by index, checked against the manifest committed when the slot was opened.

specs.title: Chat — Direct message
specs.summary: One person writes a message to another they have a relationship with — and, as its author, edits it, withdraws it, or reacts to a message — using the same content vocabulary as a room record, carried without a proof over an end-to-end binding.

specs.title: Chat — Message
specs.summary: A conversational message between an AI agent and a messaging-platform bridge, signed by its author and hash-linked to the previous message to form a verifiable per-conversation chain for audit and dispute resolution.

specs.title: Config — Patch
specs.summary: Write per-key overrides into a maintainer's runtime configuration, reporting which took effect, which await a restart, and which were rejected.

specs.title: Config — Reload
specs.summary: Re-apply hot-reloadable configuration to the running maintainer without a restart, reporting which keys changed live.

specs.title: Config — Restart
specs.summary: Request a graceful restart so a process supervisor brings the maintainer back up with restart-gated configuration applied; refuses when no supervisor is present.

specs.title: Config — Show
specs.summary: Read the effective value of a maintainer's runtime configuration keys, each with the layer it came from and whether changing it needs a restart.

specs.title: Confirm — Request
specs.summary: A relying party asks a wallet (or any consent agent) to obtain user confirmation for a specific action; the wallet returns a signed confirm/response that is the cryptographic record of the user's decision.

specs.title: Confirm — Response
specs.summary: An approver's signed answer to a confirm/request — the proof on this document is the cryptographic record of the user's decision.

specs.title: Consent — Approve Request
specs.summary: An agent's home service asks a designated human approver to decide whether the agent may act on one conversation, issuing the challenge that binds their answer to this request.

specs.title: Consent — List Approvers
specs.summary: Fetch the approver bindings that decide inbound-messaging consent, optionally filtered by platform or context.

specs.title: Consent — Set Approver
specs.summary: An admin binds the operator who approves inbound-messaging consent for a platform within a context, and how the prompt reaches them.

specs.title: Consent — Decision
specs.summary: An approver allows or denies an AI agent's access to a messaging conversation, recording a consent grant at the Verifiable-Trust Agent.

specs.title: Consent — List
specs.summary: A bridge fetches the consent grants it should enforce, so the steady-state inbound path is a local lookup with no per-message round-trip.

specs.title: Consent — Request
specs.summary: A messaging bridge asks a Verifiable-Trust Agent whether an inbound conversation may proceed to an AI agent, prompting operator consent on first contact.

specs.title: Consent — Revoke
specs.summary: An operator revokes a standing consent grant so a previously-allowed messaging conversation no longer reaches the AI agent.

specs.title: Credential Exchange — Issue
specs.summary: Issuer to holder — the issued credential, either cleartext to a known holder or as a sealed bundle only the holder can open.

specs.title: Credential Exchange — Offer
specs.summary: Issuer to holder — an OID4VCI Credential Offer that opens an issuance thread, leaving the credential format to be negotiated rather than fixed by the envelope.

specs.title: Credential Exchange — Pending Approve
specs.summary: Approve a deferred presentation request, minting the presentation against the verifier's original query and nonce and returning it to the approver.

specs.title: Credential Exchange — Pending Deny
specs.summary: Refuse a deferred presentation request. Nothing is presented, the deferral is retired, and the verifier learns nothing about why.

specs.title: Credential Exchange — Pending List
specs.summary: List the presentation requests this holder deferred for consent, showing who asked, why, and exactly which claims answering would disclose.

specs.title: Credential Exchange — Present
specs.summary: Holder to verifier — an OID4VP vp_token disclosing exactly the consented claims, bound to the verifier's nonce and audience.

specs.title: Credential Exchange — Query
specs.summary: Verifier to holder — a DCQL query with a freshness nonce and a mandatory stated purpose, which the holder answers, defers for consent, or refuses.

specs.title: Credential Exchange — Request
specs.summary: Holder to issuer — an OID4VCI Credential Request carrying the key-binding proof that ties the credential to be issued to a key the holder controls.

specs.title: Device — Disable
specs.summary: Disable a Companion or Service; the maintainer revokes its ACL entry and refuses subsequent authentication, but does not actively instruct the device to wipe its cache.

specs.title: Device — Heartbeat
specs.summary: Periodic check-in from a Companion or Service that refreshes lastSeenAt, carries optional state digests, and lets the maintainer deliver queued operations (queued wipes especially).

specs.title: Device — List
specs.summary: List DeviceBindings (Companions and Services) registered on the maintainer, optionally filtered by kind, capability, status, or last-seen time.

specs.title: Device — Register
specs.summary: A newly-onboarded Companion or Service claims its device record on the maintainer, supplying form factor, display name, HPKE public key, and optional device attestation; wraps the maintainer's existing provision-integration → acl/swap-key bootstrap.

specs.title: Device — Set Wake
specs.summary: A device tells its VTA the opaque WakeHandle it obtained from a push gateway, so the VTA can own the trigger allowlist and provision the gateway. Idempotent; carries no platform push token.

specs.title: Device — Wipe
specs.summary: The maintainer issues a wipe to a Companion or Service. Target destroys its cache (and optionally device-local keys); the maintainer additionally revokes ACL access and rotates the device's cache-key derivation root so defence in depth neutralises non-compliant targets.

specs.title: DID Management — Check Agent Name
specs.summary: A prospective claimant asks a hosting service whether an agent name (`/@alice`) is free to claim on a hosting domain — a read-only availability probe that distinguishes taken, reserved, and free.

specs.title: DID Management — Disable Agent Name
specs.summary: Park an agent name — stop it resolving while keeping it reserved to this DID. The submitted DID document must no longer claim it via `alsoKnownAs`.

specs.title: DID Management — Enable Agent Name
specs.summary: Return a parked (disabled) agent name to live resolution. The submitted DID document must claim it again via `alsoKnownAs`.

specs.title: DID Management — List Agent Names
specs.summary: A DID owner reads the authoritative agent-name registry for a hosted DID — every name bound to it, including parked entries that the DID document itself cannot show.

specs.title: DID Management — Remove Agent Name
specs.summary: Release an agent name from a hosted DID. The name stops resolving and becomes claimable by anyone. The submitted DID document must no longer claim it via `alsoKnownAs`.

specs.title: DID Management — Agent Name Resolve
specs.summary: A DID owner or an administrator asks which agent names a batch of hosted DIDs currently serve — the reverse of the `/@name` redirect — seeing only DIDs they may read.

specs.title: DID Management — Set Agent Name
specs.summary: Bind a human-memorable agent name (`/@alice`) to a hosted DID, or update an existing binding. The submitted DID document must claim the name via `alsoKnownAs`.

specs.title: DID Management — Update Agent Name
specs.summary: Set the binding state of a human-memorable agent name (`/@alice`) on a hosted DID — `active` binds, refreshes, or resumes it; `parked` stops it resolving while keeping the reservation. Supersedes the separate set / enable / disable verbs.

specs.title: DID Management — Change Owner
specs.summary: The current owner of a DID slot transfers ownership to a different VID.

specs.title: DID Management — Check Name
specs.summary: A prospective DID owner asks a hosting service whether a given path is available, and optionally — in the same round-trip — reserves it; or asks the host to auto-assign and reserve a fresh path.

specs.title: DID Management — Delete
specs.summary: A DID owner soft-deletes a hosted DID — the slot is taken off the public resolution path but content is retained for the host's recovery window.

specs.title: DID Management — Disable
specs.summary: A DID owner (or admin) suspends hosting for a DID without deleting it — resolution returns a deactivation marker but content is retained.

specs.title: DID Management — Enable
specs.summary: Inverse of `did/disable` — a previously suspended DID slot is returned to live resolution.

specs.title: DID Management — Info
specs.summary: A caller reads the canonical metadata record the hosting service holds for a single DID slot.

specs.title: DID Management — List
specs.summary: A caller enumerates DID slots they can see — their own when non-admin, or any/by-owner when admin.

specs.title: DID Management — DID Log
specs.summary: A DID owner or an administrator reads the full history a hosting service holds for a slot — every entry, parsed — and, on request, the stored log and witness artifacts verbatim.

specs.title: DID Management — Problem Report
specs.summary: A hosting service emits a problem report to an owner when an async background operation on the owner's slot fails after the original transport has closed.

specs.title: DID Management — Publish
specs.summary: A DID owner uploads a signed log entry (or full log chain) for an existing reserved slot, completing the two-step reserve-then-publish flow.

specs.title: DID Management — Register
specs.summary: A DID owner asks a hosting service to atomically claim a path and publish a signed DID log under it in one step, replacing the two-step reserve-then-publish flow for the common case.

specs.title: DID Management — Rollback
specs.summary: A DID owner reverts the slot's log chain to a prior published version, discarding the entries above that point.

specs.title: DID Management — Set State
specs.summary: A DID owner (or admin) sets a hosted DID's hosting state — `active` for live resolution, `suspended` to serve a deactivation marker while content is retained. Supersedes the separate enable / disable verbs.

specs.title: DID Management — Domain Assign
specs.summary: An administrator binds a hosting domain to a registered server instance — the bound server commits to serving DIDs on that domain.

specs.title: DID Management — Domain Create
specs.summary: An administrator adds a new hosting domain to a DID hosting service.

specs.title: DID Management — Domain Disable
specs.summary: An administrator disables a hosting domain — existing DIDs remain readable for the host's grace period, but no new DIDs may be hosted under it.

specs.title: DID Management — Domain Enable
specs.summary: An administrator re-enables a previously-disabled hosting domain, cancelling any pending purge and restoring it to active service.

specs.title: DID Management — Domain List
specs.summary: An administrator enumerates every hosting domain a DID hosting service knows — active and disabled, with each one's purge schedule — and the system default.

specs.title: DID Management — Domain Purge
specs.summary: An administrator force-removes a disabled hosting domain, bypassing the standard grace period and optionally fanning a purge directive out to every server instance currently serving the domain.

specs.title: DID Management — Domain Set Default
specs.summary: An administrator promotes a hosting domain to be the system default — every operation that omits an explicit domain resolves to this one (subject to the per-caller ACL default tier in front of it).

specs.title: DID Management — Domain Set State
specs.summary: An administrator sets a hosting domain's service state — `active` restores it to service (cancelling any pending purge), `disabled` moves it to read-only with a purge grace period. Supersedes the separate enable / disable verbs.

specs.title: DID Management — Domain Unassign
specs.summary: An administrator removes the binding between a hosting domain and a server instance — the instance stops serving DIDs on that domain after the ack round-trip.

specs.title: DID Management — Domain Update
specs.summary: An administrator updates the metadata of an existing hosting domain (label only — the `name` itself is immutable).

specs.title: DID Management — Identity List
specs.summary: An administrator lists the generations of a DID hosting service's own identity that it still honours — the current one and each superseded one, with when it stops being honoured.

specs.title: DID Management — Identity Retire
specs.summary: An administrator makes a DID hosting service stop honouring a superseded generation of its own identity immediately, dropping that generation's key material ahead of its grace period — the kill switch for a compromised key.

specs.title: DID Management — Me / Domains
specs.summary: An authenticated caller asks a hosting service for the subset of hosting domains it is permitted to act on, plus the caller's default.

specs.title: DID Management — Registry Admin Register
specs.summary: An administrator manually inserts a server instance into the control-plane registry — used to seed a known instance from configuration before the instance has had a chance to self-register.

specs.title: DID Management — Registry Check
specs.summary: An administrator asks the control plane to re-evaluate one instance now — recompute its health verdict and re-resolve the services its DID document advertises — and returns the refreshed entry.

specs.title: DID Management — Registry Deregister
specs.summary: An administrator removes a server instance from the control-plane registry.

specs.title: DID Management — Registry Get
specs.summary: An administrator reads one service instance's record from the control-plane registry — its DID, type, health verdict, served domains and the transports it was last seen on.

specs.title: DID Management — Registry List
specs.summary: An administrator enumerates the service instances registered with a control plane — hosting servers, witnesses and watchers — with each one's health verdict, served domains and transport observations.

specs.title: DID Management — Registry Purge Domain
specs.summary: An administrator tells the control plane to have one hosting server delete, now, every DID it holds on a domain that has been unassigned from it — bypassing the server's unassignment grace period.

specs.title: DID Management — Replica Domain Assign
specs.summary: A control plane tells a hosting server it drives to start serving a hosting domain, cancelling any purge the server had scheduled for it.

specs.title: DID Management — Replica Domain Purge
specs.summary: A control plane tells a hosting server it drives to delete, now, every DID it holds on a hosting domain — refused if the server has been re-assigned the domain since the directive was issued.

specs.title: DID Management — Replica Domain Unassign
specs.summary: A control plane tells a hosting server it drives to stop serving a hosting domain; the server schedules the domain's content for deletion after its grace period.

specs.title: DID Management — Replica Domain Upsert
specs.summary: A control plane replicates its record of one hosting domain — its label, state and purge schedule — to a hosting server it drives, which makes its own copy match.

specs.title: DID Management — Server Config
specs.summary: An administrator reads a DID hosting service's effective, non-secret configuration — its identity, transports, DID methods, session lifetimes, registry and storage settings.

specs.title: DID Management — Server Health
specs.summary: A liveness probe between control plane and a registered server — replaces the legacy `health-ping`/`health-pong` pair with one task and `#response`.

specs.title: DID Management — Server Info
specs.summary: Anyone asks a DID hosting service for the public facts a client needs before it has a session — the service's own DID, whether it serves agent names, and the names its own DID serves.

specs.title: DID Management — Server Metrics
specs.summary: An administrator reads a DID hosting service's operational metrics snapshot: named counters, gauges and histograms, for a metrics collector to scrape over a Trust Task instead of a Prometheus endpoint.

specs.title: DID Management — Server Register
specs.summary: A hosting server announces itself to the control plane, declaring which hosting domains it serves and where it can be reached.

specs.title: DID Management — Server Stats Sync
specs.summary: A hosting server pushes a delta of its resolve/update counters to the control plane since the last sync.

specs.title: DID Management — Stats Get
specs.summary: A DID owner reads the resolve and update counters of a slot they own, or an administrator reads those of any slot or the hosting service's server-wide aggregate.

specs.title: DID Management — Stats Set Resolution
specs.summary: A DID owner chooses less statistical detail for a slot they own, down to totals only, or an administrator chooses any level for any slot, including always keeping the finest series.

specs.title: DID Management — Stats Timeseries
specs.summary: A DID owner, a domain-scoped caller or an administrator reads resolve and update counts over a recent window, bucketed — for one slot, one domain or the whole hosting service.

specs.title: External Accounts — Archive
specs.summary: A manager archives an external account: hidden from default listings, refused for use, restorable.

specs.title: External Accounts — Bindings — Grant
specs.summary: A manager allows one integration to use an external account, up to a scope ceiling, a credential lifetime and a rate; a grant for an already-bound integration replaces its binding.

specs.title: External Accounts — Bindings — Revoke
specs.summary: A manager stops one integration using an external account, at once and alone; credentials already issued lapse at their expiry.

specs.title: External Accounts — Create
specs.summary: A manager creates an external account; the key custodian generates its key itself and returns the public material and the provider-side setup to perform.

specs.title: External Accounts — Delete
specs.summary: A manager deletes an archived external account: its record, wrapped keys and secrets are destroyed and its derived key path is retired for good.

specs.title: External Accounts — Get
specs.summary: A manager, or a bound integration, reads one external account: settings, public material, bindings, state and last probe, never a key or secret.

specs.title: External Accounts — Keys — Rotate
specs.summary: A manager rotates an external account's key in three steps — stage a successor beside the current key, confirm once the provider trusts it and a probe succeeds, or abandon — so the account never stops working.

specs.title: External Accounts — List
specs.summary: A manager, or a bound integration, lists the external accounts a key custodian holds in a context: settings, public material, bindings and state, never a key or secret.

specs.title: External Accounts — Probe
specs.summary: A manager has the key custodian prove an external account works end to end — sign, exchange at the provider, and put, get and delete one canary object at the narrowest bound scope — and records the result.

specs.title: External Accounts — Restore
specs.summary: A manager restores an archived external account to `suspended`, from which resuming it is a separate, consented step.

specs.title: External Accounts — Resume
specs.summary: A manager returns a suspended external account to use; consented, because it restores authority.

specs.title: External Accounts — Secret — Set
specs.summary: A manager sets or replaces the secret of a static external account, sealed in the manager's own client to a single-use wrapping key the custodian issued; the value is never returned, only a keyed fingerprint.

specs.title: External Accounts — Setup
specs.summary: A manager obtains, generated by the key custodian, exactly what to configure at the provider for an external account: certificates, key sets, policies and the commands that apply them.

specs.title: External Accounts — Suspend
specs.summary: A manager suspends an external account — the kill switch: every issuance and signature is refused at once, by one person, without consent.

specs.title: External Accounts — Update
specs.summary: A manager changes an external account's label or provider settings; the model and the key cannot change.

specs.title: External Credentials — Issue
specs.summary: A bound integration obtains a short-lived provider credential from an external account: a session or token downscoped to one prefix, or up to 64 presigned requests on one object, each write bound to its length and SHA-256, multipart included, sealed to the caller.

specs.title: External — Sign
specs.summary: A bound integration has a key custodian sign a Sui transaction from an external account, only after the custodian has decoded it and checked every call, object, gas budget and coin movement against the account's allow-list and caps.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — Link Forge Account
specs.summary: A member begins linking their account on a forge to their DID, so the bridge can give them the forge roles their rights call for. The response says where to authorise; the member polls git-ns/account/link-status.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — Forge Account Link Status
specs.summary: A member asks where a forge account link they began stands: pending, linked, expired or failed.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — List Linked Forge Accounts
specs.summary: A community administrator lists every member's forge account linked through git-ns/account/link, community-wide, since a member's own view of git-ns/view returns only their own.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — Unlink Forge Account
specs.summary: A member removes the link between their DID and their account on one forge. The VTC deletes the binding and re-projects, so the bridge withdraws the forge roles it gave that account; the member's git rights are unchanged.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — List Activity
specs.summary: An administrator lists recent rights changes, drift reports and bridge jobs in the namespaces they administer — every namespace, for a community administrator — newest first.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — Bridge Event
specs.summary: The bridge tells the VTC what happened on the forge — renames, transfers, role and protection changes, lost access, completed links and bindings, opened pull requests — with the drift it sees, and its role map. A namespace the VTC no longer has is orphaned on the bridge.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — Bridge Job
specs.summary: The VTC asks its bridge — the separate service holding the community's forge credentials — to do one convergent piece of forge work: project roles, create, bootstrap, archive or inspect a repository, begin a binding or account link, or close a disallowed pull request.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — List Bridge Jobs
specs.summary: An administrator lists the bridge jobs queued or run in the namespaces they administer — every namespace, for a community administrator — with each job's kind, queue state and last error.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — Bridge Job Result
specs.summary: The bridge reports how a job ended — succeeded, failed or partial, per step — and the repository's forge id, so the VTC can activate it, record its bootstrap status, or retry.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — Resolve Drift
specs.summary: An owner of a repository, or a namespace admin over it, resolves one reported drift item: adopt records the forge-side role as a VTC right for the member the resolver names, as git-ns/right/grant would; revert has the bridge undo the forge-side change.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — Bind Namespace
specs.summary: A VTC administrator binds the VTC to one owner on one forge, so the VTC governs repositories there. In bridge mode the namespace stays pending until the administrator proves control of the owner on the forge; in manual mode it is bound at once.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — List Namespaces
specs.summary: An administrator lists the namespaces they administer — every one, for a community administrator — with each one's admins, repository count, bridge, role map and what the bridge last reported about the forge.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — Reseat Namespace
specs.summary: Recovery for a headless bound namespace, one left with no live git.ns.admin: a community administrator grants git.ns.admin on it to a current member. Refused unless the namespace is headless, and recorded with the administrator's statement of why.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — Unbind Namespace
specs.summary: A namespace admin ends the VTC's governance of a namespace: every right inside it is revoked and withdrawn from the Trust Registry, and every repository in it becomes detached.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — Show Trust Registry Projection
specs.summary: A community administrator reads what the VTC has published to the Trust Registry for its git namespaces, and how many records the next reconciliation pass will still add, remove or replace.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — Adopt Repository
specs.summary: A namespace admin brings an existing forge repository under the VTC's governance and names its owners — for repositories created outside the VTC, or to finish one a person had to create by hand.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — Archive Repository
specs.summary: An owner archives a repository: the forge makes it read-only and the VTC revokes every commit-signing right on it.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — Create Repository
specs.summary: A holder of git.repo.create creates a repository and names its owners. A creator owns it only when their git.repo.create is an explicit record, never when it is implied by git.ns.admin. A bridge creates it, or the response lists manual steps.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — List Repositories
specs.summary: An administrator lists the repositories in the namespaces they administer — every one, for a community administrator — with owners, right counts, bootstrap and sync status, and what the bridge last reported on each.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — Transfer Repository Ownership
specs.summary: An owner hands their ownership of a repository to someone else: the recipient becomes an owner and the caller's own record is revoked, atomically.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — Break Glass
specs.summary: A member records for themselves an elevated git right they may already grant — the one self-grant separation of duties forbids — with a justification. It takes effect at once, never lapses, and is shown to every other administrator until one ratifies or revokes it.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — Break-Glass Notice
specs.summary: The VTC tells each administrator of a namespace, unprompted and at once, that a member broke the glass on an elevated git right — who, what, where and why — and later that the break-glass was ratified or revoked.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — Grant Right
specs.summary: A member grants one git right on one forge-qualified resource — an elevated one only to someone else. The VTC checks it against the actor's own rights and fixed rules no policy can loosen, separation of duties among them, records it, and publishes it to its Trust Registry.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — Rights Issued By Departed Members
specs.summary: A community administrator lists the recorded git rights whose granter has since left the community, grouped by granter, so they can review or revoke what an absent person authorised.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — List Rights
specs.summary: A community administrator lists every git right the VTC knows of — recorded rights and v0.1 role-derived grants alike — across every namespace, with the membership facts the console shows.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — Ratify Break-Glass
specs.summary: An administrator other than its subject ratifies an unratified break-glass record, turning a self-granted elevated right into an ordinary grant that is no longer flagged and counts toward the last-owner and last-admin invariants.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — Revoke Right
specs.summary: The granter, an authority over the resource, the subject — or, for an unratified break-glass record, any community administrator — revokes one git right. The VTC keeps an owner and an admin in place, and withdraws the right from the registry and the forge.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — Re-project Roles
specs.summary: A community administrator, a namespace admin, or a repository's owner has the VTC send its bridge the complete forge roles of a repository or a whole namespace again, so the forge matches the VTC's rights under the bridge's current role map. No right changes.

specs.title: Git Namespaces — View
specs.summary: A member reads the namespaces, repositories and git rights they may see, and their own linked forge accounts. An administrator may read everything in the namespaces they administer, and either may narrow the answer to break-glass records.

specs.title: Git Trust — Grant Commit-Signing Trust
specs.summary: A community operator grants a member's DID the authority to sign git commits for an org or repository; the host records it as a TRQP authorization tuple CI verifiers query.

specs.title: Git Trust — Revoke Commit-Signing Trust
specs.summary: A community operator revokes a member's commit-signing grant; the host marks the TRQP tuple unauthorized (retained for audit) so CI verifiers observe the denial on their next query.

specs.title: Governance — Disable Capability
specs.summary: A community operator disables a previously enabled capability; its handlers stop, it leaves discovery, and its lifecycle hooks stop firing, while its registry records are retained for audit.

specs.title: Governance — Enable Capability
specs.summary: A community operator enables a pluggable capability (its Trust Task handlers, registry vocabulary, lifecycle hooks, and management surfaces) for a community.

specs.title: Governance — List Capabilities
specs.summary: A community member or surface queries which pluggable capabilities a community has enabled (or has available), with their manifests, to render management and status views.

specs.title: Keys — Create
specs.summary: A producer asks a key custodian to generate a new key and hold it, receiving only the public half.

specs.title: Keys — Derive and Sign
specs.summary: A producer asks a custodian to derive a key at a given path and sign with it in one step, without the key being added to the custodian's stored key set.

specs.title: Keys — Derive and Sign Document
specs.summary: A producer hands a custodian a JSON document; the custodian derives a key at a path, canonicalizes the document and returns it with a Data Integrity proof attached.

specs.title: Keys Export Secret
specs.summary: Release the private half of one named key to a caller entitled to it.

specs.title: Keys — Import
specs.summary: A producer hands an externally-created private key to a custodian, which stores it and thereafter exercises it like any key it generated.

specs.title: Keys — Import Wrapping Key
specs.summary: A producer about to import a private key asks the custodian for a fresh, short-lived, single-use public key to seal it to, so the key stays confidential over a transport that is not end to end.

specs.title: Keys — List
specs.summary: A producer enumerates the keys a custodian holds, optionally filtered by lifecycle state or scope, paged by cursor so a partial page is never mistaken for the whole set.

specs.title: Keys — Rename
specs.summary: A producer changes the identifier a custodian addresses a key by, leaving the key material untouched.

specs.title: Keys — Revoke
specs.summary: A producer retires a key from further use; the record is kept so signatures it already made remain attributable.

specs.title: Keys Set Exportability
specs.summary: Mark a key as releasable to callers, or refuse every future export of it.

specs.title: Keys — Show
specs.summary: A producer asks a key custodian for the record it holds for one key, receiving the public half and lifecycle state.

specs.title: Keys — Sign
specs.summary: A producer asks a key custodian to sign a supplied byte string with a named key it holds, without the private key ever leaving the custodian.

specs.title: Keys — Sign CSR
specs.summary: A producer obtains a PKCS#10 certificate signing request for a key the custodian holds — so a certificate authority can certify a key that never leaves the custodian — with the custodian building the request from structured subject attributes and the key's own public key.

specs.title: Keys — Sign Document
specs.summary: A producer obtains a Data Integrity proof (eddsa-jcs-2022) over a JSON document from a key the custodian holds — a credential issued as a group or community DID — with the custodian building the proof and signing only as the DID the document names.

specs.title: Keys — Sign JWS
specs.summary: A producer obtains a compact JWS — a signed OpenID4VP request object, a proof-of-possession JWT — from a key the custodian holds, with the custodian building the protected header and signing input itself, so the key never leaves and the custodian signs nothing but JWS.

specs.title: Keys — Sign SSHSIG
specs.summary: A producer obtains an SSHSIG signature — the format git uses for SSH commit and tag signing — over a message digest, from a key the custodian holds, without the private key leaving the custodian and without the custodian becoming a general signing oracle.

specs.title: Messaging — Add to Access List
specs.summary: An administrator adds one or more DIDs to a served account's access list — the per-account set of other DIDs that, combined with the account's accessListMode, governs who may send to that account.

specs.title: Messaging — Clear Access List
specs.summary: An administrator empties a served account's access list — removing every entry from the per-account set of other DIDs that, combined with the account's accessListMode, governs who may send to that account.

specs.title: Messaging — Check Access List Membership
specs.summary: A requester checks whether specific DIDs are present in a served account's access list — the per-account set of other DIDs that, combined with the account's accessListMode, governs who may send to that account.

specs.title: Messaging — List Access List
specs.summary: A requester pages through a served account's full access list — the per-account set of other DIDs that, combined with the account's accessListMode, governs who may send to that account.

specs.title: Messaging — Remove from Access List
specs.summary: An administrator removes one or more DIDs from a served account's access list — the per-account set of other DIDs that, combined with the account's accessListMode, governs who may send to that account.

specs.title: Messaging — Update Access List
specs.summary: An administrator modifies a served account's access list in one task — clear it, add entries, and remove entries — replacing the separate add, remove, and clear tasks.

specs.title: Messaging — Add Account
specs.summary: An administrator registers a new served account at the mediator, declaring the account's DID and optional role, access-control capabilities, and queue limits.

specs.title: Messaging — Change Account Queue Limits
specs.summary: An administrator sets a served account's send and receive queued-message limits, applying a partial update where -1 means unlimited and an omitted member leaves that limit unchanged.

specs.title: Messaging — Change Account Type
specs.summary: An administrator changes a served account's role, with assignment or modification of the rootAdmin role reserved to a rootAdmin.

specs.title: Messaging — Get Account
specs.summary: A requester fetches the mediator's view of one served account — its role, access-control capabilities, queue limits, and current queue state.

specs.title: Messaging — List Accounts
specs.summary: A requester lists the accounts served by the mediator, paginated by an opaque cursor and a bounded page limit.

specs.title: Messaging — Remove Account
specs.summary: An administrator removes a served account from the mediator, refusing to remove protected mediator or rootAdmin accounts.

specs.title: Messaging — Update Account
specs.summary: An administrator applies a partial update to a served account — role, access-control capabilities, and queue limits in one task; a member omitted leaves that facet of the account unchanged.

specs.title: Messaging — Get ACL
specs.summary: An administrator reads the mediator's access-control capability flags for one or more served accounts, retrieving the full realized MediatorAcl capability set for each known account in a single batch query.

specs.title: Messaging — Set ACL
specs.summary: An administrator sets the mediator's access-control capability flags for a served account, applying a partial update of named capabilities (send, receive, forward, anon-receive, protocol enablement, self-manage, blocked).

specs.title: Messaging — Add Admins
specs.summary: An administrator grants admin rights to one or more accounts at the mediator.

specs.title: Messaging — Audit Log
specs.summary: An administrator pages through the mediator's privileged-change audit log, newest first.

specs.title: Messaging — Get Configuration
specs.summary: An administrator reads the mediator's current configuration and software version.

specs.title: Messaging — List Admins
specs.summary: An administrator lists the mediator's administrator accounts, paginated by an opaque cursor.

specs.title: Messaging — Strip Admins
specs.summary: An administrator removes admin rights from one or more accounts.

specs.title: Messaging — Delete Messages
specs.summary: Delete up to 100 named messages from one account's mediator queues, with a per-message result — the owner deleting its own, or an administrator clearing another account's.

specs.title: Messaging — Get Message
specs.summary: Fetch one stored message from a mediator queue, verbatim and undecrypted, together with its metadata — an account's own message, or, for a rootAdmin, any account's.

specs.title: Messaging — List Messages
specs.summary: An account controller, or an administrator, pages through the metadata of the messages in one account queue — sender, recipient, size, age, protocol, and delivery state — never their content.

specs.title: Messaging — Message Status
specs.summary: A sender asks its mediator where the messages it sent now stand — still queued, handed over, collected by the recipient, withdrawn, or discarded — so that delivery can be confirmed on evidence rather than inferred from an outbox entry disappearing.

specs.title: Messaging — Traffic Monitor Event
specs.summary: One-way batch of traffic-metadata events — and, for a subscription that opted in, mux membership events — pushed by a mediator to a live monitor subscriber, sequence-numbered so gaps are detectable and heartbeated so a dead tap is visible.

specs.title: Messaging — Subscribe to Traffic Monitor
specs.summary: Open or renew a leased, filtered, live tap on a mediator's traffic metadata — what arrives, what leaves, over DIDComm or TSP, and what was refused and why — and, only when asked, on mux membership changes, delivered as messaging/monitor/event batches.

specs.title: Messaging — Unsubscribe from Traffic Monitor
specs.summary: End a traffic-monitor subscription before its lease lapses, and learn how many events it delivered and dropped.

specs.title: Messaging — Mux Ack
specs.summary: A principal acknowledges frames delivered on its mux connection; the mediator deletes each one the principal, or the member it was for, may delete.

specs.title: Messaging — Mux Admin List
specs.summary: An administrator lists the stored mux grants of a principal DID or of a member DID a page at a time — each grant's parties, state, scope, expiry and epoch, and the member's current epoch — without the signed statements.

specs.title: Messaging — Mux Admin Revoke
specs.summary: An administrator revokes stored mux grants of other accounts — every grant of a principal DID, of a member DID, or between the two, or named grants of a member — detaching affected members from every connection, with reason admin, before the mediator answers.

specs.title: Messaging — Mux Admin Revoke All
specs.summary: An administrator advances a member DID's epoch at the mediator without the member's signature, voiding every grant on it, ending its session attaches, and detaching it from every principal, with reason admin, before the mediator answers.

specs.title: Messaging — Mux Attach
specs.summary: A principal attaches member DIDs to its authenticated connection for this session only, each by a statement the member DID signs with an embedded Data Integrity proof, bound to that one connection; every member is answered on its own.

specs.title: Messaging — Mux Connections
specs.summary: An administrator lists a mediator's live mux connections a page at a time — each connection's principal, wire and opening time, and the member DIDs it carries with their source, scope, expiry and whether their live delivery is active there.

specs.title: Messaging — Mux Detach
specs.summary: A principal removes session attaches from its mux connection; the members' live traffic stops before the mediator answers. Stored grants are untouched.

specs.title: Messaging — Mux Event
specs.summary: Live, unstored events from a mediator to the principal of one mux connection: ready (with the connection's nonce and limits), members attached, members detached with a reason, and inbound frames refused in-band.

specs.title: Messaging — Mux Grant
specs.summary: Store or replace stored grants: a member DID signs once that a principal may carry its messages, bound to the member's current key and epoch, with an explicit scope and expiry; reconnects then cost one authentication.

specs.title: Messaging — Mux List
specs.summary: List mux delegations a page at a time: as a principal, the grants delegated to it and the attaches on this connection; as a member DID, the principals holding grants on it and its current epoch.

specs.title: Messaging — Mux Notice
specs.summary: Durable notices a mediator stores in a principal's or member DID's inbox, delivered at least once and acknowledged by deletion: grants suspended (recreate them), grants revoked, grants expiring, grants present on a DID.

specs.title: Messaging — Mux Revoke
specs.summary: Revoke stored grants by identifier or by counterparty DID, as their principal or as their member DID; affected members are detached from every connection before the mediator answers.

specs.title: Messaging — Mux Revoke All
specs.summary: The hand-over switch: a member DID proves current control with a signed revoke-all statement and advances its epoch at the mediator, voiding every grant on it at once, ending its session attaches, and detaching it from every principal before the mediator answers.

specs.title: Messaging — Mux Update
specs.summary: Narrow a stored grant — a smaller scope or an earlier expiry — without a new member signature, from either side; anything that widens is refused and must be a fresh grant.

specs.title: Messaging — Ping
specs.summary: A liveness and capability check against a messaging endpoint — a mediator or an agent; the requester asks "are you there?" and the endpoint answers with its server time, health status, and the transport protocols it supports.

specs.title: Messaging — List Queues
specs.summary: An administrator ranks a mediator's accounts by the depth, size, age, or saturation of one of their queues, to find the accounts whose queues are backing up.

specs.title: Messaging — Purge Queue
specs.summary: An account controller, or an administrator, removes the messages in one account queue — optionally only those exchanged with one counterparty or older than an age — with a dry run to preview the count first.

specs.title: Messaging — Show Queue Status
specs.summary: An account controller, or an administrator, reads one account's receive and send queues — depth, size, age, limits, and optionally which counterparties account for them.

specs.title: Messaging — Receipt
specs.summary: When a sender asks for one, the recipient's delivery layer tells it that the message is durably held at the far end, by echoing the delivery id the sender stamped — end-to-end evidence of delivery that works across mediators, where a mediator's status answer cannot.

specs.title: Messaging — Show Mediator Statistics
specs.summary: An administrator reads a mediator's operational telemetry — version, uptime, connections, lifetime traffic counters, forwarding and circuit-breaker state, and the aggregate of its latest queue survey.

specs.title: Messaging — Wake Request
specs.summary: A sender that has just queued mail for a DID asks that DID's own mediator to ring the device — so a party with no standing at the device can get it woken, while the mediator alone decides, nothing about the message travels, and the answer reveals nothing.

specs.title: Messaging — Wake Set
specs.summary: An account gives its own mediator the opaque wake handle its push gateway issued, or takes it back, so the mediator can ring the account's device when a sender with mail queued for it asks — without the mediator ever holding a push token.

specs.title: Notifications — Notify
specs.summary: Tell the party a DID names — an individual, group, community or network — that a thing exists which it, or those it stands for, may take part in: where it is held, how to open it, whom it concerns. Signed by the originator, so it can be relayed and still verified.

specs.title: Notifications — Relay
specs.summary: A group, community or network passes a notification it was addressed to on to one of the parties it stands for, carrying the originator's signed document unchanged so the final recipient can verify who originated it.

specs.title: Peer Check — Ask
specs.summary: One party asks another a short yes-or-no question, such as "did you just ask me for this?", over a channel they already have; the other party's device prompts its user, and the signed answer lets the asker verify it against the responder's DID.

specs.title: Persona Attribute — Delete
specs.summary: A holder removes one fact from their attribute pool; the removal is refused while any profile still references it, unless the holder explicitly cascades, so that deleting one fact never silently changes what a profile discloses.

specs.title: Persona Attribute — Get
specs.summary: A holder reads one attribute they already hold, by identifier, optionally at a retained earlier version — so revealing a single value does not mean enumerating every attribute that shares its vocabulary prefix.

specs.title: Persona Attribute — List
specs.summary: A holder enumerates their own attribute pool, narrowed by vocabulary prefix and paginated, with values withheld unless explicitly requested so a picker can render the pool without decrypting every fact in it.

specs.title: Persona Attribute — Promote
specs.summary: A holder makes values typed into a context-local face reusable across their faces. The face moves above contexts, keeping its id and every place it is worn; the step is one-way.

specs.title: Persona Attribute — Purge Version
specs.summary: A holder permanently removes earlier versions of an attribute that their agent kept because a profile pins them — the explicit override on retention, for a value they want gone even where a face still asks for it.

specs.title: Persona Attribute — Put
specs.summary: A holder writes one atomic fact about themselves into their agent's attribute pool, declaring where the value came from, and receives back an advisory count of how many of their other profiles already present the same value.

specs.title: Persona Binding — Get
specs.summary: An application in a context learns whether a persona has a profile bound and what the holder calls it, and never what it contains.

specs.title: Persona Binding — List
specs.summary: An application enumerates the bindings in its own context — which personas operate here and what each presents — and learns nothing about anywhere else the holder operates.

specs.title: Persona Binding — Set
specs.summary: A holder assigns a profile to a persona DID in a context, or clears it; this is the push that carries a composition across the context boundary, and it is the family's critical authorization gate.

specs.title: Persona Claim Types — List
specs.summary: Serve the claim-type registry an agent resolves against, so a client reads the table rather than shipping a copy of it.

specs.title: Persona Contact — Delete
specs.summary: Remove a contact and its revisions, reporting honestly how many survived because a disclosure record still references them.

specs.title: Persona Contact — Get
specs.summary: Read one contact at its current or a named earlier revision, with the holder's own star, petname, lists and directory link — annotations only the holder's agent ever holds.

specs.title: Persona Contact — List
specs.summary: Enumerate a context's contacts as summaries with the holder's own stars, petnames, lists and directory links, narrowed by persona, star, list, community or what changed — with no claim values in the listing.

specs.title: Persona Contact Lists — Delete
specs.summary: Delete one of the holder's own contact lists and take every contact off it, leaving the contacts themselves untouched; a repeated delete converges.

specs.title: Persona Contact Lists — List
specs.summary: Enumerate the holder's own contact lists in one context, in the order they chose, with how many contacts each holds.

specs.title: Persona Contact Lists — Put
specs.summary: Create, rename, recolour or reorder one of the holder's own contact lists — kept by the holder's agent, never visible to the people on it or to any community.

specs.title: Persona Contact Lists — Show
specs.summary: Read one of the holder's own contact lists by its identifier, with a definite notFound when the context does not hold it.

specs.title: Persona Contact — Put
specs.summary: A holder's agent files what a peer disclosed as a new revision, never overwriting — and keeps the holder's own star, petname, lists and directory link on the contact, which never leave the agent.

specs.title: Persona Correlation — Analyze
specs.summary: Report where the holder's identities link to one another, why, whether the link crosses a part of their life they keep separate, and what can be done about each — including the remedy a holder would not otherwise think of.

specs.title: Persona Disclosure — History
specs.summary: What the holder has shared, with whom and when — and which contexts a given attribute has reached, which is the account the agent-scoped pool owes them.

specs.title: Persona Disclosure — Present
specs.summary: Produce the signed disclosure a preview described, consuming the preview so that a disclosure can never occur without the summary having been produced first.

specs.title: Persona Disclosure — Preview
specs.summary: Determine exactly what a disclosure would reveal, to whom, at what proof strength and through which renderer — signing nothing and sending nothing, so that no disclosure can occur without first producing the summary a human can be shown.

specs.title: Persona — Facet Delete
specs.summary: A holder removes one of the parts of their life they had named, leaving every face and attribute that belonged to it exactly where it was.

specs.title: Persona — Facet List
specs.summary: A holder reads back the parts of their life they have named, with the faces and attributes belonging to each, cursor-paginated so a client that follows the cursor sees all of them.

specs.title: Persona — Facet Put
specs.summary: A holder names a part of their life — Work, Home, Play — and says which faces and attributes belong to it, so a wallet can arrange a pool it has outgrown and can warn when one part of a life shares a value with another.

specs.title: Persona Local Binding — Set
specs.summary: Bind a context-local profile to a persona in the same context — safely context-callable, because both objects live below the boundary.

specs.title: Persona Local Profile — Delete
specs.summary: Remove a context-local profile, refusing while a persona is bound unless the caller unbinds.

specs.title: Persona Local Profile — Get
specs.summary: Read one context-local profile.

specs.title: Persona Local Profile — List
specs.summary: Enumerate a context's local profiles from an address space that structurally cannot contain a pool profile.

specs.title: Persona Local Profile — Put
specs.summary: An application composes a throwaway profile inside its own context from values it supplies, with pool references refused — which is what keeps the local surface pool-free.

specs.title: Persona Profile — Compose
specs.summary: A holder composes a face for one context at the moment it is asked for, from values typed there and attributes already held, local by default, and may wear it in the same act.

specs.title: Persona Profile — Delete
specs.summary: A holder removes a profile; the removal is refused while a persona is bound to it, unless the holder explicitly unbinds, so no persona silently stops presenting anything.

specs.title: Persona Profile — Get
specs.summary: A holder reads one profile, either as composed or resolved against the pool into the claims it would actually present.

specs.title: Persona Profile — List
specs.summary: A holder enumerates their profiles as composed, paginated, with no option to resolve — because resolving every profile at once would decrypt the whole pool to answer a question about names.

specs.title: Persona Profile — Put
specs.summary: A holder composes a named projection over their attribute pool, referencing facts rather than copying them, with four entry forms covering reuse, pinning, per-profile override and profile-local values.

specs.title: Persona Profile — Reinstate
specs.summary: A holder makes a retired face wearable again. It comes back worn nowhere — the bindings retiring cleared are not restored.

specs.title: Persona Profile — Retire
specs.summary: A holder stops being a face everywhere without destroying it — taken off every persona, hidden from pickers, unwearable until reinstated, with its values and disclosure history kept.

specs.title: Persona Profile — Timeline
specs.summary: A holder reads what one face has done, in order — composed, worn and taken off, what it told whom, when a value it shows changed, retired — with no value and no private label anywhere in it.

specs.title: Persona Profile — Usage
specs.summary: A holder asks where one of their faces is worn now — every context and persona wearing it, with the face's reach beside the answer.

specs.title: Persona Renderers — List
specs.summary: Enumerate the output formats an agent can present in, and what each discards, so a client negotiates format rather than discovering lossiness afterwards.

specs.title: Persona — World Delete
specs.summary: A holder removes one of the parts of their life they had named, leaving every face and attribute that belonged to it exactly where it was.

specs.title: Persona — World List
specs.summary: A holder reads back the parts of their life they have named, with the faces and attributes belonging to each, cursor-paginated so a client that follows the cursor sees all of them.

specs.title: Persona — World Put
specs.summary: A holder names a part of their life — Work, Home, Play — and says which faces and attributes belong to it, so a wallet can arrange a pool it has outgrown and can warn when one part of a life shares a value with another.

specs.title: Policy — Activate
specs.summary: Make a policy module the single active policy for a named decision slot (purpose), atomically deactivating whatever was active before and returning the displaced id.

specs.title: Policy — Active
specs.summary: Read the policy currently active for a purpose decision slot — the active binding for one purpose, or every active binding. The read companion to policy/activate.

specs.title: Policy — Delete
specs.summary: Delete a Rego policy module; takes effect on the next request evaluation.

specs.title: Policy — Evaluate
specs.summary: Dry-run a policy decision against a synthetic PolicyInput; returns the decision plus a trace of which modules matched and which rules fired.

specs.title: Policy — Get
specs.summary: Fetch a single Rego policy module by id, including its source. The read-one companion to policy/list.

specs.title: Policy — List
specs.summary: List Rego policy modules registered on the maintainer, optionally filtered by context or enablement status.

specs.title: Policy — Upsert
specs.summary: Create or update a Rego policy module on the maintainer. New policies take effect on the next request evaluation; no restart required.

specs.title: Process Attestation
specs.summary: Evidence that an artifact was produced through a captured process, attested by the party that captured it and bound to a Verifier-supplied challenge.

specs.title: Provision — Integration
specs.summary: A relayer presents a VP-signed bootstrap request from an integration holder; the maintainer mints the integration's DIDs and admin credential from a registered DID template and returns the material in a sealed bundle the holder can open.

specs.title: Provision — VTA Claim
specs.summary: A wallet claims a VTA that a Farm reserved behind a vta-claim trigger link, with a fresh key that becomes the VTA's administrator; the Farm locks the reservation to that key and points the wallet at redeem for the hand-over.

specs.title: Provision — VTA Redeem
specs.summary: The claimant polls the Farm with the key that claimed a reservation and, once the person has confirmed the claim check and the key is in the VTA, receives the hand-over: the VTA's DID, what the claim did and where the VTA is reachable.

specs.title: Push — Provision
specs.summary: The controller VTA sets a wake handle's trigger allowlist on the push gateway — the DIDs (its mediator and/or itself) permitted to wake the device. The gateway enforces it.

specs.title: Push — Register
specs.summary: A device registers its platform push token with a push gateway and receives an opaque WakeHandle, naming a controller VTA or — where the gateway admits it — itself as the party that sets who may wake it. The token stays at the gateway.

specs.title: Push — Wake
specs.summary: A trigger (the device's mediator or its VTA) asks the push gateway to deliver a contentless wake to a handle. The gateway authorizes against the VTA-provisioned allowlist, then fires the doorbell.

specs.title: Registry — Authorization Query
specs.summary: A relying party asks a trust registry whether an entity is authorized by an authority for a given action and resource, per the ToIP Trust Registry Query Protocol (TRQP) v2.0.

specs.title: Registry — Rotate DID Keys
specs.summary: An administrator rotates the keys of a trust registry's own agent-managed did:webvh in place, preserving the registry's DID while refreshing its key material.

specs.title: Registry — Recognition Query
specs.summary: A relying party asks a trust registry whether an entity is recognised by an authority for a given action and resource, per the ToIP Trust Registry Query Protocol (TRQP) v2.0.

specs.title: Registry — Create Record
specs.summary: An administrator records, in a verifiable form, a new recognition or authorization assertion in a trust registry.

specs.title: Registry — Delete Record
specs.summary: An administrator deletes, in a verifiable form, a recognition or authorization record from a trust registry.

specs.title: Registry — List Records
specs.summary: An administrator lists all trust records held by the registry.

specs.title: Registry — Put Record
specs.summary: An administrator creates or replaces, in a verifiable form, the recognition or authorization record at a trust registry key — one task for both halves of the superseded create/update pair.

specs.title: Registry — Query Records
specs.summary: An administrator fetches one trust record by its full four-part key, or enumerates matching records with cursor pagination — one task for both halves of the superseded read/list pair.

specs.title: Registry — Read Record
specs.summary: An administrator reads the full stored trust record for a given key, including both the recognition and authorization facets.

specs.title: Registry — Update Record
specs.summary: An administrator updates, in a verifiable form, an existing recognition or authorization record in a trust registry.

specs.title: Rooms Blobs — Chunk
specs.summary: A member fetches one chunk of a blob download they opened, and checks it against the manifest on arrival.

specs.title: Rooms Blobs — Get
specs.summary: A member opens a download of one file's ciphertext from a data room: to a room-issued chain conferring read, the host returns the blob's manifest and either a short-lived URL for that one object at storage, or a handle for fetching its chunks through the host.

specs.title: Rooms Blobs — Upload — Abort
specs.summary: A blob upload is cancelled — by its single-use key (proxied) or its owner (direct); the host discards its staged chunks and releases its reservation.

specs.title: Rooms Blobs — Upload — Begin
specs.summary: A member opens an upload of one file's ciphertext into a data room, committing to its size and digests and reserving space against every limit; the host answers with how the bytes move — straight to storage over per-part URLs, or through the host.

specs.title: Rooms Blobs — Upload — Chunk
specs.summary: An upload's single-use key sends one chunk of an open blob upload by index, checked on arrival against the digest committed for that index.

specs.title: Rooms Blobs — Upload — Commit
specs.summary: A blob upload is completed: the host reassembles it (proxied) or checks the object at storage (direct) against what begin committed, records it, and returns the BlobRef a record can then name.

specs.title: Rooms — Changed
specs.summary: A room's host tells the address of an armed watch that the room has moved past the version its member had read to, or last heard of — the room and its latest version, nothing about what changed, and no response.

specs.title: Rooms — Create
specs.summary: An owner registers a data room with a host, naming the room's own identifier, its visibility, the party accountable for it, how long it keeps its records, and whether its watch signals are delayed.

specs.title: Rooms Epoch Chain
specs.summary: A member fetches a room's epoch key chain from its host, so records sealed before they joined can still be opened — and learns the room's epoch floor, below which nothing may be kept.

specs.title: Rooms Epoch — Commits
specs.summary: A member fetches the MLS commits a room made while they were away, so they can catch up without the owner sending to each of them.

specs.title: Rooms Epoch — Mint
specs.summary: A room's owner advances its key epoch, which is how a member is removed: the new key is distributed only to those who remain.

specs.title: Rooms Epoch — Prune
specs.summary: A room's owner asks its host to drop the epoch key chain below an epoch, making the history before it unrecoverable — and the host keeps the resulting floor, so members' key holders forget what they hold below it.

specs.title: Rooms — Info
specs.summary: A member asks a room's host what it holds about the room — tier, epoch, retention and last prune, signal delay, file limits, the largest record and file chunk it accepts, and the room's and member's usage — authorized by the room's own credentials.

specs.title: Rooms Keys — Act
specs.summary: A member's own client asks the party holding the member's keys to complete one host-bound room request, or one request to a community about the rooms it offers the member, as the member — authority narrowed to the one action — and hand it back to send.

specs.title: Rooms Keys — Backfill
specs.summary: A member asks their own agent to fetch the room's epoch key chain from its host and keep it, so history written before they joined becomes readable — and to forget whatever the room has since pruned.

specs.title: Rooms Keys — Browse
specs.summary: A member asks their own agent to list a room's records at its host, oldest or newest first, between two versions, a page at a time if asked, check it against what the host committed to, and say whether records were pruned; each row says when, and by whom, it was first stored.

specs.title: Rooms Keys — Chain
specs.summary: A member hands their key-holding agent the room's epoch key chain, so it can open records sealed before they joined — and the room's epoch floor, below which it keeps nothing.

specs.title: Rooms Keys — Changed
