specs.summary: A member's key holder passes a room host's content-free signal on to the client that asked it to watch the room — the room, the member, the host and the room's latest version, nothing about what changed, and no response.

specs.title: Rooms Keys — Commit
specs.summary: A room's owner delivers an MLS Commit to a member's key-holding agent, advancing it one epoch; every member must apply every commit, in order.

specs.title: Rooms Keys — File Key
specs.summary: A member's own client asks the holder of the member's room keys for one file's key — bound to the room, the epoch and the file, opening that file and nothing else — so file bytes never pass through the key holder.

specs.title: Rooms Keys — Key-Package
specs.summary: An invited party asks the agent that will hold its room keys for the MLS KeyPackage the room's owner adds — the one it already holds for that room, member and invitation, or a new one — so an acceptance begun in one surface can be finished in another.

specs.title: Rooms Keys — Label
specs.summary: A member keeps their own private name, description, notes and tags for a room they hold, with their key holder, for their eyes only — never sent to the room, its host or a community.

specs.title: Rooms Keys — List
specs.summary: An agent asks which rooms its principal's key holder can open, as which member, how far back each one reads — and, if it asks, what the member has named each one and how far they have read it, for themselves.

specs.title: Rooms Keys — Open
specs.summary: An agent asks the party holding its principal's room keys to open one sealed record; the plaintext comes back and the key never does.

specs.title: Rooms Keys — Present
specs.summary: An agent asks the party holding its principal's room credentials to produce a presentation for one room operation, scoped to that action and granted to the agent that asked.

specs.title: Rooms Keys — Profile — Read
specs.summary: A member asks their own agent what a room is called and what it is for: the agent finds the room's profile where only members can compute it, fetches and opens it as the member, and returns the newest one whose author could write it.

specs.title: Rooms Keys — Profile — Write
specs.summary: A member holding curate or admin asks their own agent to set a room's name and description: the agent signs the profile as the member and seals it into the room where only members can find it, so members see what the room is and its host cannot.

specs.title: Rooms Keys — Read
specs.summary: A member asks their own agent to fetch one record, or up to 32, from the room's host, check what the host asserted about each, and open them — each key answered on its own.

specs.title: Rooms Keys — Read Marker — Moved
specs.summary: A member's key holder tells the member's other clients watching a room that the member's read marker for it moved — the room, the member and the marker, so a device can clear what its member already read elsewhere — and no response.

specs.title: Rooms Keys — Read Marker — Set
specs.summary: A member's client tells their key holder where the member has seen a room's conversation up to, so that every one of their devices agrees on what is unread — kept for the member alone, never sent to the room, its host or another member.

specs.title: Rooms Keys — Seal
specs.summary: A writer asks the party holding its principal's room keys to seal one record — a note, a message or a reaction — and, when the writer is the principal's own client, to sign its body as the principal first; ciphertext comes back and no key leaves.

specs.title: Rooms Keys — Watch
specs.summary: A member's client asks its key holder to watch rooms at one host for it — arming rooms/watch as the member at an address the key holder controls, one-shot or live while a conversation is open — and to pass the signals on, so a wallet need not poll.

specs.title: Rooms Keys — Welcome
specs.summary: A room's owner delivers an MLS Welcome to the agent that will hold a new member's room keys, authorized by the invitation the room already issued.

specs.title: Rooms Owner — Anchor
specs.summary: A room's owner writes the room's current epoch authenticator, version watermark and data commitment into its witnessed log.

specs.title: Rooms Owner — Claim
specs.summary: A nominated successor claims ownership of a room whose owner has stopped renewing it — an act, never an automatic promotion.

specs.title: Rooms Owner — Group — Add
specs.summary: A room's owner asks their own agent to admit a member to the room's MLS group: add their KeyPackage, advance the room's epoch at its host, and hand back the Welcome to deliver.

specs.title: Rooms Owner — Group — Create
specs.summary: A room's owner asks their own agent to form the room's MLS group, with the owner as its first member, so a sealed room can be written to before anyone else has joined.

specs.title: Rooms Owner — Group — Remove
specs.summary: A room's owner asks their own agent to remove a member from a sealed room: on an `attributed` room withdraw every credential the room gave them, in force at its host at once, and on either sealed tier drop their leaf from the room's MLS group and advance the room's epoch.

specs.title: Rooms Owner — Group — Renew
specs.summary: A room's owner asks their own agent to renew a sealed room: advance its MLS group with a commit that changes no membership, and advance the room's epoch at its host with that commit, so the room stays writable without anyone joining or leaving.

specs.title: Rooms Owner — Invite
specs.summary: A room's owner mints an invitation credential in the room's own name, so joining is a two-party act rather than something done to a member.

specs.title: Rooms Owner — Issue Authority
specs.summary: A room's owner grants a party the authority to read, write, curate or administer the room — a chain root at the room's own scope.

specs.title: Rooms Owner — Issue Membership
specs.summary: A room's owner mints the membership credential that lets a member re-enter, issued in the room's own name.

specs.title: Rooms Owner — Register
specs.summary: A room's owner asks their own agent to register the room with a host, so a surface that can reach its agent and nothing else can finish creating a room — and is told whether the room's revocation list is in force there.

specs.title: Rooms Owner — Revoke
specs.summary: A room's owner asks their own agent to withdraw credentials the room issued: sign the room's next revocation list as the room, keep it, and deliver it to every host serving the room, which refuses them from then on.

specs.title: Rooms Owner — Transfer
specs.summary: A room's owner hands ownership to another member, deliberately and while still present.

specs.title: Rooms Records — Curate
specs.summary: A member changes a record's standing in a data room — demote, retract, restore, pin — without rewriting it, under an authority action distinct from write.

specs.title: Rooms Records — Get
specs.summary: A member reads one record from a data room, presenting the same authority chain a write presents and needing no host session; the record names the stored blobs it keeps alive, and when it was first stored and by whom.

specs.title: Rooms Records — List
specs.summary: A member lists record metadata in a data room — never bodies — oldest or newest first, between two versions, with prefix, watermark and cursor, including the blobs each record names, when each was first stored, any prune, and on an open room each record's kind.

specs.title: Rooms Records — Prune
specs.summary: A room's administrator asks its host to remove the records the room's stated record retention makes eligible — old tombstones, old records, or both — leaving a mark that records went and never what they said.

specs.title: Rooms Records — Put
specs.summary: A member writes a record to a data room — a note, a message or a reaction, optionally answering another and carrying a file — authorized by an authority chain the room itself issued rather than by anything the host stores; on an open room all of it is in the clear.

specs.title: Rooms Records — Retention — Set
specs.summary: A room's administrator changes how long the room keeps its records by age — the rule every member can read, and the only one a prune may remove records under.

specs.title: Rooms Revocations — Get
specs.summary: An administrator of a data room reads the revocation list its host holds and enforces — to confirm a withdrawal reached the host, or to recover the room's list after losing it.

specs.title: Rooms Revocations — Put
specs.summary: An administrator of a data room delivers the room's signed revocation list to its host, which refuses every withdrawn credential — and everything delegated from one — from the moment it accepts the list.

specs.title: Rooms — Signal Delay — Set
specs.summary: A room's administrator changes whether the room's host waits a randomised interval before it sends a watch signal — on by default, off for a room where members expect to see a write at once, such as a conversation.

specs.title: Rooms — Usage
specs.summary: A room's owner reads, from the room's host, how much storage each member who has added files is using against their allowance — authorized by a room-issued chain conferring `admin`, and refused on `private` rooms, where the host cannot tell members apart.

specs.title: Rooms — Watch
specs.summary: A member asks a room's host for a content-free signal at an address it chooses when the room moves past the version it has read to: one per arming, or, on a room that sends signals at once, live — one per change for a few minutes, while a conversation is open.

specs.title: Sync — Event
specs.summary: One-way push notification from the maintainer to a subscribing consumer, carrying a single vault/ACL/policy change event. Pairs with vault/sync/0.1 for offline catch-up.

specs.title: Task Consent — Decision
specs.summary: An enrolled approver authorizes or refuses one pending privileged task, bound to the exact payload shown, optionally backed by an extra factor (a passkey assertion or a signed approver statement). The proof by the approver's own DID is the authorization.

specs.title: Task Consent — Granted
specs.summary: A fire-and-forget notice from the executor to the requester that its pending task has reached the approval threshold and a single-use grant is waiting, so the requester re-submits immediately instead of polling.

specs.title: Task Consent — Request
specs.summary: An executor asks an enrolled approver device to authorize one pending privileged task, presenting the effects it computed by dry-running the real handler against its own prior state.

specs.title: Trust Ceremony Receipt
specs.summary: Evidence that one enactment of a Trust Ceremony completed — the steps it comprised, in order, attested by a recorder the definition names.

specs.title: Trust Task Control
specs.summary: The framework-defined request by which a producer cancels, suspends, or resumes work a consumer has already accepted. Cancellation prevents future effects; it never undoes past ones, and the response reports what already occurred.

specs.title: Trust Task Discovery
specs.summary: Query a Trust Task party for the set of task types it supports, and the acceptance window it applies to them.

specs.title: Trust Task Error
specs.summary: The framework-defined response type a consumer returns when it cannot or will not act upon a received Trust Task document.

specs.title: Trust Task Next Step
specs.summary: The framework-defined response a consumer returns when a task was understood but cannot complete in isolation, naming the Trust Task it expects in order to proceed.

specs.title: Trust Task OK
specs.summary: Retired. The courtesy acknowledgement a consumer MAY return for a task defining no success-response document of its own — deprecated at framework 0.5.0, which lets such a task be acknowledged with an empty `#response` instead. Producers still accept one; consumers stop sending.

specs.title: Vault Credentials — Archive
specs.summary: Hide a stored credential from default query results and refuse it for presentation, reversibly.

specs.title: Vault Credentials — Delete
specs.summary: Move a stored credential to a recoverable tombstone, or erase it outright.

specs.title: Vault Credentials — Get
specs.summary: Fetch one stored credential's full body by id, for presentation.

specs.title: Vault Credentials — Present
specs.summary: Present one stored credential to a verifier the consumer names, bound to that verifier and its nonce, disclosing only the named claims — so a client that holds no holder key can still carry a presentation to a verifier itself.

specs.title: Vault Credentials — Purge
specs.summary: Erase a stored credential immediately and irrecoverably.

specs.title: Vault Credentials — Query
specs.summary: A filtered, body-free search over the credentials a holder's agent stores; claim bodies are never returned.

specs.title: Vault Credentials — Receive
specs.summary: A holder's agent verifies a received W3C credential and stores it in the credential vault.

specs.title: Vault Credentials — Restore
specs.summary: Return a soft-deleted credential to the active state, while its grace window lasts.

specs.title: Vault Credentials — Unarchive
specs.summary: Return an archived credential to the active state.

specs.title: Vault — Delete
specs.summary: A vault consumer tombstones a vault entry; the maintainer keeps the tombstone for a grace period so late-syncing consumers wipe their caches before garbage collection.

specs.title: Vault — Get
specs.summary: A vault consumer fetches the metadata view of a single vault entry by id; secret material is never returned.

specs.title: Vault — List
specs.summary: A vault consumer queries a vault maintainer for the metadata view of stored credentials, filtered by context, binding target, secret kind, tag, last-used time, expiry, or breach status; secrets are never returned by this task.

specs.title: Vault — Proxy Login
specs.summary: A vault consumer asks the vault maintainer to perform a login at the bound third-party site on the holder's behalf, returning a session blob the consumer can use without ever seeing the long-term credential.

specs.title: Vault — Release
specs.summary: A vault consumer requests the cleartext secret material of an entry; the maintainer returns it inside an HPKE-sealed envelope with a strict cache TTL. The fallback when proxy-login is not viable.

specs.title: Vault — Sign Trust Task
specs.summary: A vault consumer asks the vault maintainer to attach a Data Integrity proof to a Trust Task envelope, signing as the principal DID of a `didSelfIssued` (or `didcommPeer`) vault entry. The long-term signing key never leaves the maintainer.

specs.title: Vault — Sync
specs.summary: A vault consumer requests an incremental delta of vault, ACL, and policy events since a known seq baseline; pairs with sync/event push notifications to keep local caches converged with the maintainer.

specs.title: Vault — Upsert
specs.summary: A vault consumer creates a new vault entry or updates an existing one; secret material rides inside an HPKE-sealed envelope so the Trust Task itself carries only ciphertext.

specs.title: Vault — Usage
specs.summary: A vault consumer queries the maintainer's audit log of recent credential uses (proxy-logins, releases), filtered by entry, context, consumer, kind, and time range.

specs.title: Vetting — Attestation
specs.summary: A vetter gives an applicant an attestation that carries the facts of a vetting session and names nobody, for the applicant to prove over when it applies to the community.

specs.title: Vetting — Decline
specs.summary: A vetter tells an applicant it will not issue a Vetting Statement for a request it accepted. The reason is optional, and the decline never goes to the community.

specs.title: Vetting — Request
specs.summary: An applicant asks one existing member to vet their identity for one community. The vetter accepts and shows it is eligible to vet, or refuses.

specs.title: Vetting — Session
specs.summary: A vetter opens a vetting session with an applicant it agreed to vet, while the two are together; the applicant answers with a signed Vetting Card bound to this session. The session document's id is what the resulting Vetting Statement cites as taskContext.

specs.title: Voting — Ballot Cast
specs.summary: A voter's client sends one ballot, admitted by a PCS attestation and signed by a key made for this cast alone, to the election's ballot box, which records it on the board and answers with a signed receipt.

specs.title: Voting — Ballot — Cast Encrypted
specs.summary: A voter casts a sealed or tallied-encrypted ballot, admitted by its PCS attestation and, when tallied-encrypted, by its proofs of validity.

specs.title: Voting — Board Consistency
specs.summary: Proves that an election board as one signed head commits to it is a prefix of the board as a later head commits to it — that the ballot box only appended.

specs.title: Voting — Board Head
specs.summary: Reads an election board's current signed tree head, the commitment every inclusion and consistency proof is checked against.

specs.title: Voting — Board Inclusion
specs.summary: Proves that one board entry — typically the voter's own cast — is in the board as a given signed head commits to it, with a receipt token that authorizes exactly that leaf on a private board.

specs.title: Voting — Board Read
specs.summary: Reads a page of an election board's entries — casts, replacements, lifecycle entries and the result — against the current head or an earlier one, so anyone allowed to read the board can count it again.

specs.title: Voting — Election Cancel
specs.summary: The community cancels one of its elections before voting closes; the election then admits no cast and is never tallied.

specs.title: Voting — Election Close
specs.summary: The community closes voting in one of its elections before the manifest's closing time, where the manifest allows an early close.

specs.title: Voting — Election Register
specs.summary: A community registers an election — its signed manifest and the voting key its tickets are issued under — with the ballot box the manifest names.

specs.title: Voting — Election Show
specs.summary: Reads one election at its ballot box — state, manifest digest, ballots admitted and the board's current head — with the registered manifest.

specs.title: Voting — Result Show
specs.summary: Reads an election's result once the ballot box has tallied it, or its provisional running totals while voting is open where the manifest allows them, with the head the totals count.

specs.title: Voting — Trustees — Authorize
specs.summary: After voting closes, the community authorizes the decryption of exactly the targets it computed from the board, pinned by digest to a head.

specs.title: Voting — Trustees — Confirm
specs.summary: A trustee confirms the shares it was dealt, or complains of the dealers whose shares failed their check.

specs.title: Voting — Trustees — Deal
specs.summary: A trustee publishes its contribution to the election key: commitments to its polynomial and every trustee's share sealed to that trustee.

specs.title: Voting — Trustees — Decrypt
specs.summary: After voting closes, a trustee publishes its partial decryption of every target, each with a proof it used its share of the election key.

specs.title: Voting — Trustees — Enrol
specs.summary: A trustee of a sealed or tallied-encrypted election publishes the key its shares of the election key are sealed to.

specs.title: Voting — Trustees — Justify
specs.summary: A dealer answers a complaint by publishing the share it dealt to the complaining trustee, for anyone to check.

specs.title: Voting — Trustees — Status
specs.summary: Where an election's trustee ceremony stands: transport keys, dealings, complaints, the election key, and what remains to decrypt.

specs.title: VRC Relationships — Issue
specs.summary: Delivers one party's signed Verifiable Relationship Credential to the other within an accepted relationship exchange, and returns a delivery receipt. Performed once in each direction — the exchange is mutual.

specs.title: VRC Relationships — Propose
specs.summary: One person proposes a peer-to-peer relationship to another, naming the pairwise DID they will use for it; the counterparty accepts or declines, and says whether the exchange will be witnessed. Opens the relationship exchange every later document of the exchange threads to.

specs.title: VTA Application State — Delete
specs.summary: An application deletes one of its state records from a VTA, leaving a versioned tombstone so that peers syncing incrementally learn of the deletion instead of resurrecting the record.

specs.title: VTA Application State — Get
specs.summary: An application reads one of its versioned state records from a VTA by its context, namespace and key, receiving the value together with the version a later conditional write will need.

specs.title: VTA Application State — Get Many
specs.summary: An application reads up to 256 of its state records from one namespace in a single round trip, with every requested key accounted for as found, missing, or deferred to a follow-up request.

specs.title: VTA Application State — List
specs.summary: An application enumerates its state records in a VTA context — a prefix-scoped snapshot, or an incremental change feed since a watermark that includes tombstones so a consumer's local copy converges.

specs.title: VTA Application State — Put
specs.summary: An application writes one versioned state record to a VTA, optionally conditional on the version it last read, and receives a typed conflict carrying the maintainer's current version and value when that precondition fails.

specs.title: VTA Application State — Put Many
specs.summary: An application flushes up to 64 state writes to a VTA in one round trip, each carrying its own version precondition, applied either independently so one conflict does not block the rest or atomically for records sharing an invariant.

specs.title: VTA Attestation — Config Report
specs.summary: Ask an agent for fresh attestation evidence that commits to the configuration it booted, so a tenant can check the settings its operator supplied before trusting the agent.

specs.title: VTA Attestation — Mnemonic Export
specs.summary: Release a TEE agent's seed mnemonic once, sealed to the requester, over an end-to-end channel or as a request the requester signed for its own key.

specs.title: VTA Attestation — Mnemonic Status
specs.summary: A super administrator checks whether a TEE agent's one-time mnemonic export window is open, before asking for the release itself.

specs.title: VTA Attestation — Report
specs.summary: Ask an agent for fresh hardware attestation evidence, bound to a nonce the verifier chose and to the agent's DID, so the verifier can check what code the agent runs.

specs.title: VTA Attestation — Status
specs.summary: Ask an agent whether it runs in a trusted execution environment, and which kind, before relying on anything it attests.

specs.title: VTA Backup — Abort
specs.summary: Cancel an in-flight export or import bundle and discard its bytes.

specs.title: VTA Backup — Complete Export
specs.summary: Acknowledge that an export bundle was downloaded, so the agent can release it.

specs.title: VTA Backup — Finalize Import
specs.summary: Decrypt an uploaded bundle and replace this agent's state with it.

specs.title: VTA Backup — Get Chunk
specs.summary: Retrieve one chunk of a chunked export bundle by index, over the transport that carries the rest of the family.

specs.title: VTA Backup — Initiate Export
specs.summary: Mint an encrypted full-state export bundle and return the descriptor that fetches it, over HTTPS or chunk by chunk over the agent's own Trust Task transport.

specs.title: VTA Backup — Initiate Import
specs.summary: Mint an upload slot for an encrypted bundle and return the descriptor that writes to it, over HTTPS or chunk by chunk over the agent's own Trust Task transport.

specs.title: VTA Backup — Put Chunk
specs.summary: Write one chunk of a chunked import bundle by index, checked against the manifest committed when the slot was opened.

specs.title: VTA Collection — Claim
specs.summary: A client asks its VTA to make it, until a stated end, the one collector of the messages queued at the mediator for a persona DID whose keys the VTA holds — or renews a claim it holds — so that the client and the VTA never both hold that DID's one mediator connection.

specs.title: VTA Collection — List
specs.summary: A client lists who collects the messages queued at the mediator for each of the principal's persona DIDs in one trust context — the VTA, a claiming client and until when, or nobody and why.

specs.title: VTA Collection — Release
specs.summary: A client releases the collection claim for a persona DID — its own, ending it at once once it has stopped collecting, or another client's, which then ends at its stated end without renewal — so that the VTA collects for the DID again.

specs.title: VTA Collection — Settings — Set
specs.summary: A context administrator enables or disables, for one trust context, whether the VTA collects the messages queued at the mediator for the persona DIDs there that no client has claimed — stored, audited, and applied at once.

specs.title: VTA Collection — Settings — Show
specs.summary: A client reads whether its VTA collects by default for the persona DIDs of one trust context that no client has claimed, who last changed that and when, and whether the VTA's operator has suspended it everywhere.

specs.title: VTA Contexts — Create
specs.summary: An administrator creates a VTA context — a new separation boundary for keys, DIDs, vault entries and policy, optionally nested under an existing one.

specs.title: VTA Contexts — Delete
specs.summary: An administrator deletes a context and everything scoped to it; refused by default while it still holds anything, or while a hosting server cannot confirm removing one of its DIDs.

specs.title: VTA Context DID-Template — Create
specs.summary: A context administrator (or super-admin) creates a DID template scoped to a context.

specs.title: VTA Context DID-Template — Delete
specs.summary: A context administrator (or super-admin) removes a context-scoped template by name.

specs.title: VTA Context DID-Template — Get
specs.summary: A caller with context access fetches one context-scoped template by name.

specs.title: VTA Context DID-Template — List
specs.summary: A caller with context access lists templates scoped to a context.

specs.title: VTA Context DID-Template — Render
specs.summary: A caller with context access renders a context-scoped template to a DID document.

specs.title: VTA Context DID-Template — Update
specs.summary: A context administrator (or super-admin) replaces a context-scoped DID template.

specs.title: VTA Contexts — Get
specs.summary: A caller fetches one VTA context by id, and learns definitively whether it exists.

specs.title: VTA Contexts — List
specs.summary: A caller enumerates the VTA contexts it can reach — the separation boundary that keys, DIDs, vault entries and policy all belong to.

specs.title: VTA Contexts — Preview Delete
specs.summary: An administrator asks what deleting a context would destroy, and is told, without anything being destroyed.

specs.title: VTA Context Secrets
specs.summary: Fetch the private key material for the DID of one trust context, so a service holding that context can operate as it.

specs.title: VTA Contexts — Update
specs.summary: A super-administrator edits a context's name, description, DID or policy; the id is fixed because ACL scopes name it.

specs.title: VTA Contexts — Update DID
specs.summary: An administrator sets or clears the DID a context acts as; existing references to the previous DID are not migrated.

specs.title: VTA Credentials — Issue
specs.summary: A context authority issues a scoped, time-boxed Verifiable Credential to a holder after operator step-up approval — the basis for an explicit, revocable cross-context share.

specs.title: VTA Credentials — List
specs.summary: Enumerate the credentials an agent has issued, as metadata. Bodies are not returned.

specs.title: VTA Credentials — Revoke
specs.summary: A context authority revokes a credential it previously issued, ending a cross-context share before its natural expiry.

specs.title: VTA DID-Template — Create
specs.summary: An administrator uploads a new DID template — global (super-admin) when contextId is absent, context-scoped (context admin) when present.

specs.title: VTA DID-Template — Delete
specs.summary: An administrator removes a DID template by name — global (super-admin) when contextId is absent, context-scoped (context admin) when present.

specs.title: VTA DID-Template — Get
specs.summary: An authenticated caller fetches one DID template by name — global when contextId is absent, context-scoped when present.

specs.title: VTA DID-Template — List
specs.summary: An authenticated caller lists the DID templates in one scope on a VTA — global when contextId is absent, context-scoped when present.

specs.title: VTA DID-Template — Render
specs.summary: An authenticated caller renders a DID template to a DID document, supplying variables — global when contextId is absent, context-scoped when present.

specs.title: VTA DID-Template — Update
specs.summary: An administrator replaces an existing DID template — global (super-admin) when contextId is absent, context-scoped (context admin) when present.

specs.title: VTA DIDs — Create
specs.summary: An administrator has a VTA create a key-role identity at key assurance level 2 or 3, under any eligible DID method, from a key-role DID template: every key minted fresh for its role and level, and at level 3 an external recovery key and a witness.

specs.title: VTA DIDs — Keys Add
specs.summary: An administrator adds a newly minted key to the attestation, operational or messaging role of a key-role identity — a post-quantum attestation key beside a classical one — under any eligible DID method.

specs.title: VTA DIDs — Keys List
specs.summary: Read the key roles of a key-role identity under any eligible DID method: each role's keys and states, the update authority and whether a recovery key is committed, and the rotation history — in a public or a custody projection.

specs.title: VTA DIDs — Keys Retire
specs.summary: An administrator retires a key of a key-role identity on schedule under any eligible DID method — completing a rotation by retiring the predecessor or aborting it by retiring the successor; a retired attestation or messaging key is destroyed.

specs.title: VTA DIDs — Keys Revoke
specs.summary: An administrator revokes a key of a key-role identity for compromise: no overlap, the compromise time published, a replacement where needed, and for the update role a move to the routine successor or, if the VTA may be compromised, to the recovery key.

specs.title: VTA DIDs — Keys Rotate
specs.summary: An administrator rotates one key role of a key-role identity: successors staged, switched in at the cache horizon, predecessors retired after an overlap. For the update role, the authority moves on or the recovery commitment is replaced.

specs.title: VTA DIDs — Recover
specs.summary: A super-administrator of a replacement VTA takes over a key-role identity whose VTA was lost: the replacement generates new keys, and the identity's recovery custodian signs the one change that reveals the recovery key, publishes the new keys, and commits fresh successors.

specs.title: VTA DIDs — Update
specs.summary: An administrator changes the non-key members of a key-role identity — services, aliases, method parameters such as witnesses — under any eligible DID method. Keys change only through the key-role tasks.

specs.title: VTA DIDs — Upgrade
specs.summary: A super-administrator raises an identity's key assurance level in place — from a single key to role-separated or recoverable, or from role-separated to recoverable — with fresh keys for every role whose custody tightens, without changing the identifier. A level is never lowered.

specs.title: VTA Health — Details
specs.summary: Ask a Verifiable Trust Agent for its public health flags — messaging, seal and storage-encryption state, trusted-execution status and transport advertisement — with a fixed answer that never identifies anyone.

specs.title: VTA Management — Reload Services
specs.summary: Re-read the agent's service configuration and restart its transports.

specs.title: VTA Memory — Delete
specs.summary: An agent forgets a memory item, leaving a tombstone so its other devices learn of the deletion, optionally only if the item is still at the version it last read.

specs.title: VTA Memory — Get
specs.summary: An agent recalls up to 256 named memory items from a VTA context in one round trip, each with its version, and learns which keys hold nothing.

specs.title: VTA Memory — List
specs.summary: An agent recalls the memory items in a VTA context a page at a time, narrowed by key prefix, or syncs a local copy with a change feed that carries deletions.

specs.title: VTA Memory — Put
specs.summary: An agent stores a memory item in a VTA context, optionally conditional on the version it last read, and receives a typed conflict carrying the current version and value when another writer got there first.

specs.title: VTA Metrics — Show
specs.summary: An administrator reads a Verifiable Trust Agent's operational metrics snapshot: named counters, gauges and histograms, for a metrics collector to scrape over a Trust Task instead of an unauthenticated Prometheus endpoint.

specs.title: VTA Notifications — Deposit
specs.summary: A client hands its VTA a notification or relay it received for a DID the VTA holds keys of — a persona DID whose mediator socket the client holds — exactly as received, and the VTA verifies and holds it exactly as if it had been delivered directly.

specs.title: VTA Notifications — Dismiss
specs.summary: A client dismisses one notification its VTA holds for the principal, taking it out of the default list without telling anyone — the originator, a relayer or the thing's holder.

specs.title: VTA Notifications — List
specs.summary: A client lists the notifications its VTA holds for the principal in one trust context — filtered by kind or holder — which, for elections, is how a member sees what they have been told they may take part in.

specs.title: VTA Notifications — Show
specs.summary: A client reads one notification its VTA holds for the principal, with the document that delivered it exactly as received, so it can verify the originator and every relay itself.

specs.title: VTA Passkey-VM — Enroll Challenge
specs.summary: An administrator of a VTA-managed DID requests a fresh WebAuthn registration challenge so a browser can create a passkey to be published as a verificationMethod on that DID.

specs.title: VTA Passkey-VM — Enroll Submit
specs.summary: An administrator submits the WebAuthn registration result for an open ceremony; the VTA re-derives the public key from the attestation, rejects browser tampering, and publishes the passkey as a verificationMethod on the DID.

specs.title: VTA Passkey-VM — List
specs.summary: An administrator enumerates the passkey verificationMethods currently published on a VTA-managed DID.

specs.title: VTA Passkey-VM — Revoke
specs.summary: An administrator removes a passkey verificationMethod from a VTA-managed DID document, identified by its URL fragment, via a WebVH log entry.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Applications — Create
specs.summary: An applicant's client asks its VTA to start a hidden-vetting application: the VTA derives a fresh PCS key for it, keeps the key, and returns the PCS identifier vetters attest to.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Applications — Delete
specs.summary: A client tells its VTA to forget a hidden-vetting application: its PCS key and every attestation it holds are destroyed.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Applications — Show
specs.summary: A client reads one of its hidden-vetting applications back from its VTA: its PCS identifier and the metadata of the attestations it holds, never its key.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Attest
specs.summary: A vetter's client asks its VTA to attest, after the human check, that an applicant was vetted: the VTA spends a token and makes an attestation that names no vetter.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Prove
specs.summary: A client asks its VTA for the zero-knowledge proof a hidden-vetting join submission carries, bound to the community's single-use challenge.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Root Accept
specs.summary: A vetter's client hands its VTA the community's answer to a root request; the VTA unblinds it into the vetter's class credential for the period and keeps it.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Root Request
specs.summary: A vetter's client asks its VTA for the blinded request that enrols the vetter with a community for a vetting period; the VTA creates the vetter's PCS key on first use and keeps the blinding state.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Tokens — Abandon
specs.summary: A vetter's client tells its VTA that the community refused a token draw, so the VTA stops holding it in flight.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Tokens — Accept
specs.summary: A vetter's client hands its VTA the community's answer to a token draw; the VTA unblinds the tokens into the vetter's wallet.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Tokens — Request
specs.summary: A vetter's client asks its VTA for one draw of the attestation-token drip: blinded serials bound to the vetter's member DID, the label and the tick.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Trustee Deal
specs.summary: The trustee's VTA deals its contribution to the election key and returns the voting/trustees/deal request signed as the trustee.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Trustee Decrypt
specs.summary: The trustee's VTA makes its partial decryption of each target, with proofs, and returns the voting/trustees/decrypt request signed as the trustee.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Trustee Enrol
specs.summary: The trustee's VTA generates the election's transport key and returns the voting/trustees/enrol request signed as the trustee.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Trustee Justify
specs.summary: The dealer's VTA reveals the share it dealt to a trustee that complained, and returns the voting/trustees/justify request signed as the dealer.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Trustee Keys
specs.summary: The trustee's VTA opens the shares it was dealt, checks each, keeps its share of the election key, and returns the voting/trustees/confirm request signed as the trustee.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Trustee Read
specs.summary: A trustee's client asks its VTA for a voting/trustees/status or voting/election/show request signed as the trustee, so it can follow the ceremony at the ballot box without holding the trustee's key.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Verify Attestation
specs.summary: A client hands its VTA an attestation a vetter sent; the VTA checks it and its token against the community's parameters and keeps it for the application's proof.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Vetter — Recover
specs.summary: A vetter's client asks its VTA to restore the vetter key a community has bound the member to. The VTA searches the keys it can derive for the context and, if one matches, makes it the engine's key — so the vetter can enrol again without an administrator's reset.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Vetter — Show
specs.summary: A vetter's client reads back its VTA's vetter engine for a community: identifier, enrolled labels, token counts and draws in flight — never its key, credentials or tokens.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Vote
specs.summary: A voter's client hands its VTA a ballot; the VTA checks it against the election's manifest, makes the ticket's attestation over it, and returns the complete voting/ballot/cast document — signed by a did:key used for this cast alone — for the client to send.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Vote Encrypted
specs.summary: The voter's VTA checks a ballot against the manifest, encrypts it to the election key as the election's level requires, and returns the cast signed by a key made for it alone.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Voter Accept
specs.summary: A voter's client hands its VTA the community's answer to a ticket request; the VTA unblinds it into the voter's ticket for the election and keeps it.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Voter Read
specs.summary: A voter's client asks its VTA for an elections list, show or tombstone read signed as the voter's membership DID — a show presenting a membership credential the member chose — so it reads as the member without the member's key.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Voter Receipt
specs.summary: A voter's client hands its VTA the ballot box's receipt for a cast, and optionally a checkpoint and an inclusion proof; the VTA checks the receipt is the voter's, keeps it, and says whether the cast is in the checkpoint.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Voter Receipts — List
specs.summary: A voter's client asks its VTA for the ballot box's receipts it keeps for one election, so that after voting closes it can check each cast against the head the community kept at close.

specs.title: VTA PCS — Voter Register
specs.summary: A voter's client asks its VTA for the blinded request that obtains the voter's ticket for one election; the VTA derives a voter key for that election alone and keeps the blinding state.

specs.title: VTA Restore — Status
specs.summary: An administrator asks a Verifiable Trust Agent whether its state derives from a backup restore — when, by whom, from which agent, and what did not come back — and which software version it runs.

specs.title: VTA Services — Disable
specs.summary: An operator stops advertising a transport; for DIDComm this begins a drain rather than cutting delivery.

specs.title: VTA Services Drain — Cancel
specs.summary: An operator ends a drain early, accepting the loss of anything still in flight.

specs.title: VTA Services Drain — List
specs.summary: An operator sees which DIDComm mediators are draining and until when.

specs.title: VTA Services — Enable
specs.summary: An operator advertises a transport, writing it into the agent's signed DID document.

specs.title: VTA Services — Get
specs.summary: An operator reads the current state of one transport.

specs.title: VTA Services — List
specs.summary: An operator enumerates the transports an agent advertises in its DID document.

specs.title: VTA Services — Report
specs.summary: An operator asks an agent which mediators its inbound traffic arrived through, and through which mediator each sender last reached it — to see who is still on the old route after a migration.

specs.title: VTA Services — Rollback
specs.summary: An operator reverts a transport to its previous settings by writing a new log entry.

specs.title: VTA Services — Update
specs.summary: An operator changes the settings of a transport the agent already advertises.

specs.title: VTA did:webs DIDs — Create
specs.summary: An administrator creates a did:webs relationship, persona or service DID (a node's durable identity, alpha) in a context, from explicit members or a DID template: the VTA derives the keys, writes the KERI v2 events, and publishes keri.cesr through a hosting server.

specs.title: VTA did:webs DIDs — Delete
specs.summary: An administrator deactivates a did:webs DID: the VTA publishes a rotation to no next keys, commits it, then removes the slot from the hosting server. Irreversible. Alpha.

specs.title: VTA did:webs DIDs — Get
specs.summary: Fetch one did:webs DID the VTA holds — its keys, designations, host and state — optionally with its keri.cesr stream. Alpha.

specs.title: VTA did:webs DIDs — List
specs.summary: Enumerate the did:webs DIDs a VTA holds that the caller may see, optionally narrowed to a context or hosting server. Alpha.

specs.title: VTA did:webs DIDs — Rotate Keys
specs.summary: An administrator rotates a did:webs DID to its pre-rotated successor and commits a fresh one. The VTA stages the rotation event, publishes it, then commits it. Alpha.

specs.title: VTA did:webs DIDs — Update
specs.summary: An administrator replaces a did:webs DID's designated services, key agreement key or designated aliases. Each is a designation anchored by an interaction event; the key state does not change. Alpha.

specs.title: VTA WebVH Agent-Name — Check
specs.summary: Ask whether an agent name is free on a host before trying to take it.

specs.title: VTA WebVH Agent-Name — Disable
specs.summary: An administrator stops an agent name resolving while continuing to hold it.

specs.title: VTA WebVH Agent-Name — Enable
specs.summary: An administrator makes a held-but-disabled agent name resolve again.

specs.title: VTA WebVH Agent-Name — List
specs.summary: List every agent name a DID holds, enabled or not.

specs.title: VTA WebVH Agent-Name — Remove
specs.summary: An administrator releases an agent name, making it available to anyone else.

specs.title: VTA WebVH Agent-Name — Set
specs.summary: An administrator binds an agent name to a DID.

specs.title: VTA WebVH DIDs — Create
specs.summary: An administrator mints a did:webvh in a context: the VTA generates the keys, writes the log's first entry, and publishes it through a hosting server or hands it back to be served.

specs.title: VTA WebVH DIDs — Delete
specs.summary: An administrator deletes a did:webvh the VTA holds; the published log may outlive the deletion, and the response says when it has.

specs.title: VTA WebVH DIDs — Get
specs.summary: Fetch one did:webvh record the VTA holds, optionally with its full log.

specs.title: VTA WebVH DIDs — Keys Add
specs.summary: An administrator asks the VTA to generate a key and add it to one role of a did:webvh — a post-quantum attestation key beside a classical one, a second operational key — without removing any.

specs.title: VTA WebVH DIDs — Keys List
specs.summary: List a did:webvh's keys by role — attestation, operational, messaging, update — with each key's state, and optionally the rotation history.

specs.title: VTA WebVH DIDs — Keys Retire
specs.summary: An administrator retires one key of a did:webvh by planned retirement — completing a rotation, aborting one, or removing an added key. What the key signed while published stays valid.

specs.title: VTA WebVH DIDs — Keys Revoke
specs.summary: An administrator revokes a did:webvh key for compromise: it leaves its role in one entry without overlap, the compromise time is recorded so verifiers stop trusting what it signed from then on, and a generated replacement takes its place where the role would otherwise be empty.

specs.title: VTA WebVH DIDs — List
specs.summary: Enumerate the did:webvh DIDs a VTA holds, optionally narrowed to a context or hosting server.

specs.title: VTA WebVH DIDs — Realign Keys
specs.summary: An administrator brings a did:webvh's key records back into agreement with the verification methods its published document declares.

specs.title: VTA WebVH DIDs — Register With Server
specs.summary: A super-administrator hands an existing DID's log to a hosting server so it is served there.

specs.title: VTA WebVH DIDs — Rotate Keys
specs.summary: An administrator rotates one key role of a did:webvh: the successor is staged, activated once every cached document can have seen it, and the predecessor retired at the end of an overlap. For the update role, the log's update key moves to its committed successor.

specs.title: WebVH DID Update
specs.summary: A caller asks a Verifiable Trust Agent to publish a new entry in a did:webvh log whose update key the agent holds — services, witnesses, watchers, TTL — with a preview of exactly what the entry will do. Keys are not changed here; they change only through the key-role tasks.

specs.title: WebVH Servers — Domains
specs.summary: A producer asks an agent which hosting domains it may use on one of the hosting servers it has registered; the agent relays the server's caller-scoped view.

specs.title: VTA WebVH Servers — List
specs.summary: Enumerate the did:webvh hosting servers a VTA is registered with.

specs.title: WebVH Servers — Reconcile
specs.summary: A producer asks an agent to compare the DIDs a hosting server holds for it against the DIDs it has records for, and to report where the two disagree.

specs.title: VTA WebVH Servers — Register
specs.summary: A super-administrator registers a did:webvh hosting server with the VTA.

specs.title: VTA WebVH Servers — Remove
specs.summary: A super-administrator removes a hosting registration; DIDs the server already serves keep resolving.

specs.title: WebVH Servers — Retire Orphan
specs.summary: A producer asks an agent to remove a slot from a hosting server after the agent has confirmed for itself that the slot is orphaned — served by the host, with no record in the agent that controls it.

specs.title: VTA Witness — Accept
specs.summary: A client hands its VTA the witness's answer to the submission — the VTA verifies the Verifiable Witness Credential against the session and stores it in the credential vault with its evidence.

specs.title: VTA Witness — List
specs.summary: A client reads back from its VTA the Verifiable Witness Credentials stored for its principal, each with the outcome evidence a verifier needs to pair it with its session.

specs.title: VTA Witness — Open
specs.summary: A client asks its VTA to open a witnessed session for one of its principal's relationships — the VTA checks custody and the credentials, and returns the witness/session document, signed as the relationship DID, for the client to send.

specs.title: VTA Witness — Present
specs.summary: A client hands its VTA the witness's answer to an opened session — the VTA verifies it is the witness's own, builds the presentations bound to its challenge, and returns the witness/session/submit document, signed as the relationship DID, for the client to send.

specs.title: VTA Witness — Request
specs.summary: A client asks its VTA to run a witnessed session for one of its principal's relationships — open the session with a named witness as the relationship DID, present the credentials it holds, verify the Verifiable Witness Credential returned, and store it with its evidence.

specs.title: VTC Admin Actions — Acknowledge
specs.summary: An administrator of a Verifiable Trust Community acknowledges an operation that took effect outside the approval path — an operator's offline or break-glass write — so that every administrator demonstrably saw it.

specs.title: VTC Admin Actions — Cancel
specs.summary: The requester of an open administrative action at a Verifiable Trust Community withdraws it, so the parked operation never executes and the action leaves every administrator's list.

specs.title: VTC Admin Actions — List
specs.summary: An administrator enumerates the Verifiable Trust Community's parked administrative actions they may see — waiting for them, requested by them, cooling off before they land, or closed — with the badge counts a console shows.

specs.title: VTC Admin Actions — Show
specs.summary: Fetch one parked administrative action of a Verifiable Trust Community by its identifier — what a requester follows after a gated operation is parked, and what an approver opens before deciding.

specs.title: VTC Admin — Bootstrap
specs.summary: Write the first admin to a community's ACL, consuming the setup-session token from install claim.

specs.title: VTC Admin Events — Event
specs.summary: A hint a Verifiable Trust Community sends down an administrator console's live channel — this topic changed, re-read it, and for badge topics the count is now n — that never carries a record, so it can neither leak data nor stand in for a read.

specs.title: VTC Admin Events — Subscribe
specs.summary: An administrator's console opens one live channel per session over which a Verifiable Trust Community sends hints — which topic changed, and for badge topics a count — never records; the console re-reads through its signed reads, and polling stays the fallback.

specs.title: VTC Admin Invites — Create
specs.summary: Invite an additional administrator to a Verifiable Trust Community — either a named DID, claimed by signing as it, or whoever registers a passkey, whose DID is derived from it — and receive the one-shot install URL and claim code.

specs.title: VTC Admin Invites — List
specs.summary: Enumerate a Verifiable Trust Community's administrator invites, outstanding and historical — wallet and passkey alike — with their redemption state.

specs.title: VTC Admin Invites — Revoke
specs.summary: Revoke an outstanding administrator invite by its `jti`, so the install URL can no longer be redeemed.

specs.title: VTC Auth — Admin Session
specs.summary: Exchange a bearer access token for an HttpOnly cookie session, so a browser administration UI can call the community without exposing the token to scripts.

specs.title: VTC Auth — Recognise
specs.summary: Mint a scoped cross-community session by presenting a foreign community's role (authority) and membership credentials; maps the foreign role to a local one via policy.

specs.title: VTC Auth Recognise — Challenge
specs.summary: Issue the single-use nonce a foreign community's member binds into the presentation they use to obtain a cross-community session.

specs.title: VTC Backup — Export
specs.summary: Export a Verifiable Trust Community's full state as a single password-encrypted envelope (Argon2id + AES-256-GCM), optionally including the audit log.

specs.title: VTC Backup — Import
specs.summary: Restore a Verifiable Trust Community from an encrypted backup envelope. Previews by default; `confirm` clears the backed-up keyspaces and applies it.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Awards — List
specs.summary: The owners' view of a badge: every award of it, open, accepted, declined, withdrawn, expired or revoked, a page at a time, each recipient projected as the directory projects them and marked where they hid the badge.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Awards — Offer
specs.summary: A badge owner offers a community badge to members, one at a time or a whole group at once: each offer is an award waiting for its recipient, and nothing is admitted or issued until they accept.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Awards — Revoke
specs.summary: Take an accepted award back: revoke or stop renewing the credential that evidences it, remove the holder from the badge group where it was their last award, and tell them.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Awards — Share
specs.summary: Show an accepted award outside the community: the holder asks, and the community answers the public locations at which it serves the award's credential, a verification of it, and the badge's picture with the credential baked in.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Awards — Unshare
specs.summary: Stop showing an award outside the community: its public locations answer nothing from now on, as if they never existed. Stopping is not a revocation; the holder keeps the award and its credential.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Awards — Withdraw
specs.summary: Withdraw an open offer of a badge before its recipient decides — by a badge's owner or a badge administrator, or by the giver of a kudos award.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Claims — Create
specs.summary: Issue a claim code for a community badge — for handing out at an event: the community generates the code, answers it once and keeps only its digest.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Claims — List
specs.summary: A badge's claim codes, as its owners and administrators see them — label, time, limit and claims — a page at a time, never a code.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Claims — Redeem
specs.summary: Redeem a claim code: the member who was there is admitted to the badge — the redemption is their consent — with an award whose giver is the code's issuer.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Claims — Withdraw
specs.summary: Withdraw a claim code: it admits no one from now on, and the claims already made stand.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Create
specs.summary: Define a badge: a community badge, which creates the badge group that backs it and names its owners, or a kudos badge a member makes for other members to give.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Holders — List
specs.summary: Who holds a badge, a page at a time, each holder projected as the directory projects them to the caller, with hidden holders left out and the count stated over those shown.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Images — Get
specs.summary: Read the bytes of a badge's picture, answered only to an active member who may see the badge.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Images — Upload
specs.summary: Hand the community the picture for a badge, which it re-encodes, strips of metadata and stores, answering the reference a badge then holds.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Kudos — Give
specs.summary: Give a kudos badge to another member: records an award offered to them, with the giver and a note, within the community's limits. The recipient accepts or declines it; nothing is issued.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Kudos — List
specs.summary: List the kudos the signer received or gave, a page at a time, each with its badge and the other party as the directory projects them; or, for a badge administrator, every giving of one kudos badge.

specs.title: VTC Badges — List
specs.summary: List the badges the caller may see — every listed active badge and the ones they hold, own or are offered; every badge for an administrator — with how many of each they hold and where they stand with it.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Mine — Accept
specs.summary: A member accepts a badge offered to them: for a community badge the badge group issues their badge credential first and admits them after; for a kudos badge the giving is counted. Nothing shows on a card until this.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Mine — Arrange
specs.summary: Arrange the signer's wall: the order of their badges, which of them are pinned beside their name, and who may see the wall. Each member absent from the request is unchanged.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Mine — Decline
specs.summary: Decline a badge offered to the signer: the offer is closed, nothing is recorded in any group and nothing is issued; the same badge may be offered again later.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Mine — Hide
specs.summary: Hide a badge the signer holds: off their wall, out of the badge's holder list and its count, out of their kudos total — while every award, the badge-group membership and the credential stand unchanged.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Mine — List
specs.summary: A member's own badges: every badge they hold, hidden ones included, in their own order, with the offers waiting for their decision, their wall visibility and their kudos total.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Mine — Show
specs.summary: Show a badge the signer had hidden: back on their wall, back in the badge's holder list and its count, back in their kudos total. The reverse of vtc/badges/mine/hide.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Promote
specs.summary: Turn a kudos badge into a community badge: its badge group is created and its owners named, and every current holder is offered the badge so that each accepts before anything is issued or recorded; the kudos awards stay as history.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Retire
specs.summary: Retire a badge: it is given to nobody again, its open offers are withdrawn, and for a community badge its status-bearing credentials are revoked and its badge group deleted; every award is kept for its holders' own history.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Settings — Show
specs.summary: Read the community's badge settings: whether badges are on, who may make a kudos badge, the limits, whether kudos totals show, whether automatic badges run and whether members may ask for a badge.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Settings — Update
specs.summary: An administrator replaces the community's badge settings: badges on or off, who may make a kudos badge, the limits, whether kudos totals show, whether automatic badges run and whether members may ask for a badge.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Show
specs.summary: Read one badge the caller may see: the badge, how many of it the caller holds and where they stand with it, its owners or its maker, and the credential regime it carries.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Update
specs.summary: Change a badge's name, description, criteria, picture, listing and, for a community badge, whether members may ask for it and who sees its holders. Its kind and credential regime are fixed at creation.

specs.title: VTC Badges — Wall — Show
specs.summary: A member's badge wall as a viewer sees it: the badges they hold and show, pinned first and then in their own order, with their kudos total where the community shows one — answered only where the directory shows the viewer that member's card and the member shows their badges.

specs.title: VTC Boards — Create
specs.summary: An administrator creates a board where members propose ideas, leave notes and vote on each accepted idea through an election of its own.

specs.title: VTC Boards — Delete
specs.summary: A board manager deletes a closed board whose voting has ended: its ideas, notes and each election's content are removed, and each election keeps only a tombstone — identifier, manifest digest and kept board heads — for the community's tombstone retention.

specs.title: VTC Boards — Facilitators — Add
specs.summary: A facilitator of a board appoints an active member a facilitator of that board — an access-control resource grant of vtc.boards.manage qualified to that board.

specs.title: VTC Boards — Facilitators — List
specs.summary: A facilitator of a board reads who is appointed to facilitate it: each appointee by entry, when and by whom they were appointed, and whether the appointment is under review.

specs.title: VTC Boards — Facilitators — Remove
specs.summary: A facilitator steps down, or a holder of vtc.boards.manage unqualified ends another member's appointment as a board's facilitator.

specs.title: VTC Boards — Ideas — Decide
specs.summary: A facilitator accepts a proposed idea — opening an election for it from the board's template — declines it, merges it into another, or moves a declined idea back to proposed.

specs.title: VTC Boards — Ideas — Propose
specs.summary: A member proposes an idea on a board, under their own name, while the board takes proposals.

specs.title: VTC Boards — Ideas — Select
specs.summary: After an idea's election is tallied, a facilitator records whether it is selected, optionally placing it in a timetable slot, with the result the decision was made with.

specs.title: VTC Boards — Ideas — Update
specs.summary: A proposer changes their idea's title, description, format or topic while it is still proposed.

specs.title: VTC Boards — Ideas — Withdraw
specs.summary: A proposer withdraws their idea while it is still proposed.

specs.title: VTC Boards — List
specs.summary: List the boards the caller may see: those whose audience admits them, and every board they facilitate.

specs.title: VTC Boards — Notes — Add
specs.summary: A member attaches a short note, under their own name, to a board or to one idea on it.

specs.title: VTC Boards — Notes — Hide
specs.summary: A facilitator hides a note on their board, with a reason the board's audience sees in its place.

specs.title: VTC Boards — Notes — List
specs.summary: List a board's notes, or one idea's, as the caller may read them.

specs.title: VTC Boards — Notes — Withdraw
specs.summary: A note's author withdraws it; its text is no longer shown to the board's audience.

specs.title: VTC Boards — Show
specs.summary: Show one board and its ideas as the caller may see them, with each accepted idea's election stage, ballot count where its board is public, and result once tallied — never who took a ticket or voted.

specs.title: VTC Boards — Update
specs.summary: A facilitator changes a board's title, description, topics, formats, timetable or selection rule, closes or archives it — which ends the voting on its ideas — or, before voting opens, its schedule; changing its election template takes an elections manager.

specs.title: VTC Ceremonies — List
specs.summary: Return the community's ceremony manifests — the declarative descriptions an operator UI renders to drive each governance decision.

specs.title: VTC Community — Branding — Show
specs.summary: Read how the community asks to be shown to a prospective applicant — a display name, an accent colour and a logo URL.

specs.title: VTC Community — Branding — Update
specs.summary: An administrator replaces how the community asks to be shown to a prospective applicant — a display name, an accent colour and a logo URL.

specs.title: VTC Community — Join Discovery — Show
specs.summary: Read whether the community answers its join manifest to a caller it cannot identify.

specs.title: VTC Community — Join Discovery — Update
specs.summary: An administrator replaces whether the community answers its join manifest to a caller it cannot identify.

specs.title: VTC Community — Logo — Show
specs.summary: Read the logo a community holds — its digest, media type, size, dimensions and the URL it is served at, and on request the bytes themselves.

specs.title: VTC Community — Logo — Update
specs.summary: An administrator hands the community a new logo, which it re-encodes, strips of metadata and serves from its own origin — or removes the one it holds.

specs.title: VTC Community Profile — Show
specs.summary: Fetch the Verifiable Trust Community's public profile (name, description, contact, language) plus live registry-reachability status.

specs.title: VTC Community Profile — Update
specs.summary: Update the community's public profile (name, description, contact, language, extensions); a partial patch, refuses to set the read-only registry status.

specs.title: VTC Community — Requested Attributes — Show
specs.summary: Read what the community asks an applicant to tell it about themselves, as persona claim types — never values.

specs.title: VTC Community — Requested Attributes — Update
specs.summary: An administrator replaces what the community asks an applicant to tell it about themselves, as persona claim types — never values.

specs.title: VTC Community — Theme — Show
specs.summary: Read the stylesheet a community's own pages — its administration console and its member portal — are drawn with.

specs.title: VTC Community — Theme — Update
specs.summary: An administrator replaces the stylesheet the community's console and member portal are drawn with — or checks one without storing it.

specs.title: VTC Config — DID Hosting — List
specs.summary: An administrator lists the did:webvh hosting servers the community's VTA can publish its identities through, to choose where its groups' and rooms' identities are published.

specs.title: VTC Config — Export
specs.summary: Export a Verifiable Trust Community's portable configuration — its profile and its stored configuration overrides — as one self-describing document.

specs.title: VTC Config — Import
specs.summary: Apply a portable configuration document to a Verifiable Trust Community, or preview what applying it would change. Previews by default.

specs.title: VTC Credentials — Reissue
specs.summary: A community administrator asks the VTC to re-sign its status lists and re-issue the credentials still in force that an attestation key revoked for compromise signed, under the community's current attestation key.

specs.title: VTC Directory — Card — Assert
specs.summary: An administrator writes the values of admin-sourced directory fields on a member's card — the facts the community asserts about a member, which the member reads and cannot change.

specs.title: VTC Directory — Card — Present
specs.summary: A member presents a credential so the community can fill credential-sourced directory fields with the disclosed claims, badged with their issuer; the community keeps the claims, never the presentation.

specs.title: VTC Directory — Card — Public
specs.summary: Read a member's external card exactly as they signed it — open to anyone, by entry, while the member keeps it published.

specs.title: VTC Directory — Card — Publish
specs.summary: A member publishes their external card — their public directory values as a JSContact card they signed — which the community serves as signed and points its trust registry to, until the values change, the member withdraws it or leaves.

specs.title: VTC Directory — Card — Show
specs.summary: A member reads their own directory card whole: every value, the visibility of each field, their discoverability and introduction settings, and its revision.

specs.title: VTC Directory — Card — Update
specs.summary: A member changes their own directory card: values they write themselves, the visibility of each field, their discoverability and who may ask to be introduced to them.

specs.title: VTC Directory — Disclosure
specs.summary: Read the statement, generated from the community's configuration, of what its directory discloses about members and to whom — readable by anyone, applicants above all, before they apply.

specs.title: VTC Directory — Entries — List
specs.summary: Browse, search and filter a community's member directory. Each entry is projected for the caller: only fields the member, the community's ceiling and its policy all allow.

specs.title: VTC Directory — Entries — Show
specs.summary: Read one directory entry, projected for the caller. Members address it by entry identifier; administrators may also address it by DID.

specs.title: VTC Directory — Export
specs.summary: A directory administrator exports the whole member directory as JSContact cards, a page at a time. Members cannot export.

specs.title: VTC Directory — Fields — Define
specs.summary: An administrator adds a field to the community's directory schema: its type, who writes it, its ceiling and its default visibility.

specs.title: VTC Directory — Fields — List
specs.summary: Read a community's directory schema — base and community-defined fields, their types, ceilings and default visibility — as the caller may see it.

specs.title: VTC Directory — Fields — Retire
specs.summary: An administrator retires a community directory field: it is hidden at once, its values are purged after the community's retention period, and its key is never reused.

specs.title: VTC Directory — Fields — Update
specs.summary: An administrator changes a directory field's label, help text, constraints, order, ceiling or default visibility, or disables or re-enables a base field.

specs.title: VTC Directory — Images — Get
specs.summary: Read the bytes of an image on a directory entry — an avatar or an image field — answered only where the caller's projection of that entry shows it.

specs.title: VTC Directory — Images — Upload
specs.summary: Hand the community an image for a directory card — an avatar or an image field — which it re-encodes, strips of metadata and stores, answering the reference a card then holds.

specs.title: VTC Directory — Introduce
specs.summary: A member asks the community to introduce them to another member's entry, offering a fresh pairwise DID to reply to. The answer is always `accepted`, so the request reveals nothing about the other member.

specs.title: VTC Directory — Introduction
specs.summary: The community delivers an introduction to a member: who asked, what they chose to share, their message, and a pairwise DID to answer them at directly.

specs.title: VTC Directory — Notes — Append
specs.summary: An administrator adds a note about a member to the community's administrative notes, or redacts an earlier note with a later one. Notes are never edited.

specs.title: VTC Directory — Notes — Export
specs.summary: An administrator exports every administrative note about one member, redacted ones included, to answer that member's subject-access request.

specs.title: VTC Directory — Notes — List
specs.summary: An administrator holding the notes capability reads the community's administrative notes about one member, newest first.

specs.title: VTC Directory — Query
specs.summary: Read the fields a community member has consented to publish, projected through the community's directory policy rather than read straight from the record.

specs.title: VTC Elections — Ballot Boxes — List
specs.summary: An administrator reads the voting services the community trusts to hold its elections' boards, with what members are told about each, so a manifest names one the community will accept.

specs.title: VTC Elections — Cancel
specs.summary: An administrator cancels an election before voting closes: the community stops issuing its tickets at once and has the ballot box cancel it, so no result is ever computed.

specs.title: VTC Elections — Certify
specs.summary: An administrator has the community verify a tallied election's board for itself — every cast's attestation, every tag counted once, the result recomputed, the board consistent with every checkpoint the community kept, no more ballots than tickets — and certify the result.

specs.title: VTC Elections — Close
specs.summary: An administrator closes voting in an election before its scheduled close, where the election's manifest allows it; the community has the ballot box close the board.

specs.title: VTC Elections — Create
specs.summary: An administrator creates a poll, survey or election of the community from its manifest; the community checks it, records it and registers it with the ballot box the manifest names, and a binding election first takes another administrator's consent.

specs.title: VTC Elections — List
specs.summary: A member or an administrator pages through the community's polls, surveys and elections the caller may see, with each one's schedule, state and whether the caller already holds its ticket.

specs.title: VTC Elections — Show
specs.summary: A member or an administrator reads one election whole — manifest and digest, state, voting parameters, disclosure, board checkpoints and certified result; a member of a party a credential roll names reads it by presenting that membership.

specs.title: VTC Elections — Tickets — Issue
specs.summary: A party the roll admits asks for its ticket, under a credential roll presenting its membership credential, which the community verifies before looking up the election; the community checks eligibility, records the issuance and blind-signs a request it cannot open.

specs.title: VTC Elections — Tombstones — Show
specs.summary: A member reads the tombstone the community keeps of an election on a deleted board — identifier, manifest digest, ballot box and the board heads it kept, each in the ballot box's signed document — so a receipt can still be checked against the community's record.

specs.title: VTC Endorsement-Types — Delete
specs.summary: Remove an endorsement type from a community's registry; refused while anything still references it.

specs.title: VTC Endorsement-Types — List
specs.summary: List the endorsement types a community recognises.

specs.title: VTC Endorsement-Types — Register
specs.summary: Register a statement predicate a community will accept — a DTG VSC registry IRI or a community-namespace IRI — optionally with a schema for the statement's object value.

specs.title: VTC Endorsements — Issue
specs.summary: A community issues a Verifiable Statement Credential under a registered predicate to a subject — an endorsement under endorses/1, or a vetted/1 statement recording its own identity check — with a published status-list slot for revocation.

specs.title: VTC Endorsements — List
specs.summary: Page through the statement credentials the community issued through vtc/endorsements/issue, optionally filtered by predicate or subject; live and revoked rows both surface.

specs.title: VTC Endorsements — Revoke
specs.summary: Revoke a community-issued statement credential, or a vetter role credential, by flipping its published status-list bit; reports alreadyRevoked on re-revocation rather than succeeding silently.

specs.title: VTC Endorsements — Show
specs.summary: Fetch one statement credential the community issued through vtc/endorsements/issue, by id, including its status-list slot and revocation state.

specs.title: VTC Groups — Bindings — Add
specs.summary: Bind a group to a community room, so its members are offered admission, or to a grant set or role's capabilities, which the community provisions into members' access-control entries with the group as their source.

specs.title: VTC Groups — Bindings — List
specs.summary: A group manager or administrator lists what a group is bound to: the rooms its members are admitted to and the grants it confers.

specs.title: VTC Groups — Bindings — Remove
specs.summary: Remove a group's binding: members lose the room admission or grants it provided, unless another source still provides them.

specs.title: VTC Groups — Create
specs.summary: An administrator creates a community group: the community's VTA mints the group's own DID and, where it issues credentials, the community authorises it to issue membership credentials; the group is recorded only afterwards.

specs.title: VTC Groups — Delete
specs.summary: A group manager deletes a group: its bindings are withdrawn first, its members' credential renewal stops and its authorization credential is revoked, and only then is the group removed.

specs.title: VTC Groups — Join
specs.summary: A member joins an open group at once, or asks to join a group that takes requests; where the group issues credentials, they are offered a membership credential issued by the group's DID.

specs.title: VTC Groups — Leave
specs.summary: A member leaves a static group, opts out of a dynamic one, or withdraws a pending request to join: renewal of their group credential stops, and what only the group provided is withdrawn.

specs.title: VTC Groups — List
specs.summary: List the community groups the caller may see — all of them for an administrator, the visible ones for a member — optionally only those they belong to or could join.

specs.title: VTC Groups — Managers — Add
specs.summary: A group manager, or an administrator who manages every group, appoints a community member a manager of one group — an access-control resource grant of vtc.groups.manage qualified to that group.

specs.title: VTC Groups — Managers — Remove
specs.summary: A manager steps down, or an administrator who manages every group withdraws another member's appointment as a group's manager.

specs.title: VTC Groups — Members — Add
specs.summary: A group manager adds a community member to a static group; where the group issues credentials, the group's DID issues the member a membership credential first.

specs.title: VTC Groups — Members — List
specs.summary: List a group's members, a page at a time, each projected for the caller as the directory projects them — only where the group shows its members to the caller.

specs.title: VTC Groups — Members — Remove
specs.summary: A group manager removes a member from a static group: renewal of their group credential stops, and room admissions and grants that only this group provided are withdrawn.

specs.title: VTC Groups — Requests — Decide
specs.summary: A group manager approves or declines a request to join; an approval admits the member, with a membership credential issued by the group's DID where the group issues credentials.

specs.title: VTC Groups — Requests — List
specs.summary: A group manager lists requests to join the groups they manage, pending by default.

specs.title: VTC Groups — Show
specs.summary: Read one community group the caller may see: its DID, name, kind, policies and, where permitted, its member count and managers.

specs.title: VTC Groups — Update
